title: e2e: let the New Folder Flow finish binding the notebook before the kernel workaround
description:
Addresses the 5.8% flake (10 of 173 ubuntu/electron runs over 14 days) in `New Folder Flow: Jupyter Project > Jupyter Folder Defaults`. Product side tracked in #16454. The spec's #14163 workaround picks a kernel (`kernel.change('Python')`) right after the console is ready. In CI that lands while the New Folder Flow's own notebook session is still starting (it starts the session first and selects the kernel only once the session is up, 3 to 4 s later on the runner). The pick fails with "cannot be started because language runtime ... is already starting for the notebook" and the idle status never appears. This change waits for one of the two product signals before the workaround runs: the kernel badge leaves "No Kernel Selected" (the binding landed), or the flow's "No notebook editor is open" warning appears (the binding was skipped, which is what happens when only the Positron notebook editor is open, see #16454). The 30 s bound covers the flow's own 10 s kernel-registration fallback on top of session startup. The workaround itself stays until #16454 is fixed; once the notebook binds reliably on its own, the test should assert the folder runtime instead of re-selecting a kernel. ### Release Notes #### New Features - N/A #### Bug Fixes - N/A ### Validation Steps @:new-folder-flow @:critical Local: 3 of 3 passes in Electron on macOS with this change (the warning-toast path). The collision path only reproduces in CI, where the legacy notebook editor tab is also open. Expected rate after merge: 0 for this failure mode; confirm on the e2e dashboard test-health view for `New Folder Flow: Jupyter Project > Jupyter Folder Defaults|||test/e2e/tests/new-folder-flow/new-folder-flow-jupyter.test.ts` over the next 14 days (about 170 ubuntu/electron runs; at the old 5.8% rate a clean streak of that length happens by luck under 0.01% of the time). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ### E2E Triage Diagnosis
🟢 High confidence -- The spec's #14163 workaround (kernel.change to the global Python) races the New Folder Flow's own notebook setup: positronNewFolderService starts the notebook session for the folder runtime first and selects the kernel only after the kernel registers (up to 10s later). A pick inside that gap throws in validateRuntimeSessionStart because the folder session is still in _startingNotebooksByNotebookUri, so the idle status never appears. - **Test:** [New Folder Flow: Jupyter Project > Jupyter Folder Defaults](https://connect.posit.it/e2e-test-insights/?tab=test_health&repo=positron&test=New%20Folder%20Flow%3A%20Jupyter%20Project%20%3E%20Jupyter%20Folder%20Defaults%7C%7C%7Ctest%2Fe2e%2Ftests%2Fnew-folder-flow%2Fnew-folder-flow-jupyter.test.ts) - **Targeted failure:** expect(.editor-action-bar-container .codicon-positron-runtime-status-idle).toBeVisible 10s - ubuntu/electron - **Signal:** renderer.log 01:32:15.230 Starting session for fa5b80 (Source: New Folder Notebook Creation); 01:32:15.279 positron-notebook-0 Unexpected session started ... Expected runtime undefined; 01:32:18.332 Session for e50104 cannot be started because fa5b80 is already starting for the notebook (stack: SelectPositronNotebookKernelAction.run); 01:32:18.98 [New folder startup] Overriding pre-selected kernel ... Kernel fa5b80 selected: exact match after polling - **Frequency:** 10/173 runs (5.8%) on main, ubuntu/electron - **Hypothesis:** Test-code race with the product's startup flow. The workaround predates the New Folder Flow's kernel auto-selection (#14163 was closed by a keyword, but the auto-bind exists: _selectKernelForNotebook). Waiting for the binding to land (or for the flow to report it skipped the notebook) before the workaround removes the collision; asserting the binding itself is blocked on #16454, because the flow finds no Positron notebook editor when the legacy tab is absent. Product side: a 3-4s window where the notebook shows No Kernel Selected over a starting session and a manual pick errors - filed separately. - **Supersedes:** #16334 (unskipped the suite keeping the workaround)

title: Say that recommended startup also starts an interpreter when needed
description:
Updates the Settings editor description for the `recommended` value of `interpreters.startupBehavior`. It now says an interpreter also starts when one is needed, such as when you open a Python or R file.

The old text said `recommended` starts an interpreter only "when the extension providing the interpreter recommends it." But opening a Python or R file also starts one. The check that runs on file open, `autoStartRuntime()` in `runtimeSession.ts`, blocks only `manual` and `disabled`. It has done that since `recommended` was added in #6145, so starting on file open looks intended.

The new text reuses the "when needed" wording from the `auto` description. It says nothing about whether the interpreter last used in the workspace starts. That part is inconsistent today, and it needs a decision first (item 2 in #16380).

Draft until the intended behavior of `recommended` is confirmed. Part of #16380.

title: e2e analyzer rubric: check request order, reconcile verdicts with the pass rate
description:
The second half of the fix for the e2e analyzer's misdiagnosis of nightly run
[35870872309](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron-builds/actions/runs/35870872309).
#16462 fixed the evidence it was missing; this PR fixes the reasoning that filled the
gap. The analyzer called the `Variables - Progress bar` failure a suspected product
regression. It was a test race, fixed test-side in #16184: the Delete All Variables
`clear` request reached the kernel 73 ms before the pasted `Sys.sleep(20)` did.

The report made four reasoning errors, and `rubric.md` (shared by the skill and the
Action) gets one rule for each:

| What the analyzer wrote | Rule added |
|---|---|
| "R kernels serialize input, so Delete is queued behind the 20s Sys.sleep, guaranteeing the session2 runtime is Busy" | **Verify the test established its own precondition** gains a third shape: assuming two requests reach the backend in the order the test issued them. A step that presses Enter has only *dispatched* its work, and the kernel serves requests in arrival order. Check the log excerpt's kernel messages (send order) and the trace's step gap rather than assuming. The console's Interrupt button is not a gate: `actionBar.tsx` shows it during the completeness check, before the execute request is sent. |
| "progress bar does not render after switching to a newly-created session" (a path the test runs every time), with "Iteration 1 succeeded, so the assertion is fundamentally sound" | New section **Reconcile the mechanism with the pass rate**: a mechanism on an always-taken path predicts a failure on every run, so 65/67 refutes it. What survives is a race; name both sides. Covers the two traps: a passing iteration in the same run does not localize a deterministic defect, and source showing how a component *could* fail is not evidence it did. The "suspected product regression" residual must fit the pass rate too. |
| "starting Sep 21 ... a rising failure rate on one platform on a specific date, which per the rubric is a regression signal" (2 occurrences, labeled `known_flaky`) | **A trend needs enough failures to be one**: two or three failures can't establish an onset; compare with what the steady rate predicts, and don't override `known_flaky` on a handful. |
| "a broad range that plausibly touches variables/session-switching code, but the individual SHAs are not resolvable" | **Submodule bumps** are assessed through the commits #16462 now lists, and **only cite changes you can see**: an unknown change set is reported as unknown, never as "plausibly touches". |

Smaller edits: the `[before deadline]` tag #16462 added is documented in "Respect the
clock" as a candidate cause, the kernel messages section is described under the log
excerpt, and an excerpt that fell back to the error grep is called out as missing
evidence that lowers confidence rather than a gap to fill with an assumed order.

### Replaying the run

To see what each half changes, I replayed the analyzer on this run's evidence. The
replay used `analyze.mjs`'s exact system and user prompts, written to files instead
of sent. The source tree was archived at the commit CI tested (`eb54319`, before the
test fix, so the answer isn't in the source). A fresh Claude subagent stood in for the
model, limited to Read/Glob/Grep inside the evidence and source directories. I ran
each cell twice; the user prompt is byte-identical between the two rubrics, so the
rubric is the only variable in each row.

| Evidence | Rubric | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| As CI had it (before #16462) | current | suspected product regression (the actual CI report) |
| As CI had it | **this PR** | test logic bug, medium-low and low confidence (2/2) |
| After #16462 | current | test logic bug (2/2) |
| After #16462 | **this PR** | test logic bug (2/2) |

- **#16462's evidence already flips this run's verdict** -- with the current rubric,
  both replays read the kernel send order and found the race. The rubric's effect
  there shows in the details:
  - Both current-rubric replays recommend gating on the Interrupt button. That is the
    fix #16184 tried first and found does not work. One also called the 2-failure
    history "may be a real onset".
  - Both new-rubric replays recommend what #16184 actually shipped: print a marker,
    `waitForConsoleContents` for it, and don't gate on the Interrupt button. Both say
    two occurrences are too few for a trend.
- **On the evidence CI actually had, the rubric alone avoids the product call.** No
  kernel messages, an error-grep excerpt, no screenshots. Both replays still reject
  "never renders for a second session" against 65/67, name the missing precondition
  gate, call the unexpanded bump "unknown", and lower their confidence for the missing
  evidence, which is the honest read there.

This is four replays per rubric on one run, not a benchmark. It shows these rules do
what they were written for; it does not show they never push a real product race the
wrong way. The pass-rate section is written so a product race stays a product bug.

title: Let agents run commands that need a particular editor, such as Shiny's Run App
description:
Fixes #16375

Posit Assistant couldn't run `shiny.r.runApp`: Positron always reported it disabled, even with `app.R` open. Assistant runs Positron commands through `positron.ai.validateAndExecuteCommand`, which checked each command's precondition against the window's context. Shiny enables the command with `editorLangId == r && shellExecutionSupported`, and `editorLangId` exists only in each editor's own context, so the check could never pass. The Command Palette and the editor's Run App button worked because they check in the editor's context.

Preconditions are now checked the way the Command Palette checks them: in the active editor's context, or the active editor group's when the editor has none of its own. This applies both when running a command and when listing which agent commands are enabled.

This isn't a code regression. Assistant has checked preconditions this way since posit-dev/assistant#1810, and Shiny's precondition dates to 2024. It surfaced when #15951 started pointing agents at `shiny.r.runApp`.

None of Positron's own agent commands change behavior, since they all depend on window-level state. The fix matters for extension commands that depend on the active editor, which today means Shiny's run commands.

The PR also corrects the positron-commands skill, which told agents that a `disabled` Shiny command meant the file wasn't recognized as a Shiny app.

### Demo

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/50cd04e9-dbea-4923-bc91-5c72fbf10e72


### Release Notes

#### New Features

- N/A

#### Bug Fixes

- Posit Assistant can now run commands that depend on the active editor, such as the Shiny extension's Run App (#16375)

### Validation Steps

@:assistant

1. Install the Shiny extension and open a Shiny for R `app.R`.
2. In Posit Assistant, outside Ask mode, ask it to run the app.
3. Assistant should run `shiny.r.runApp`, and the app should start and show in the Viewer. Before this fix, the command came back unavailable and Assistant fell back to calling `runApp()` in the console, which blocked the session.

Checked by hand with Posit Assistant and Shiny for R (see the video above). Unit tests in `agentAllowedCommandsService.vitest.ts` check Shiny's precondition against real nested context key services. They cover an R editor, a Python editor, an editor's own context winning over its group's, and the fallback to the group's context. The R-editor case fails without the fix.

title: e2e analyzer: find the real failing action, show kernel send order, restore screenshots
description:
The e2e failure analyzer called nightly run
[35870872309](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron-builds/actions/runs/35870872309)'s
`Variables - Progress bar` failure a **suspected product regression**. It was a test race,
fixed test-side in #16184: the Delete All Variables `clear` request reached the kernel
73 ms before the pasted `Sys.sleep(20)` did, so an idle kernel answered it before the
progress bar could appear.

The evidence for that was attached to the run, but the analyzer never saw it. Four
separate gaps in how it collects evidence hid it, and this PR closes them. The rubric
gaps that let it fill the hole with a product story (an assumed message order, a
deterministic verdict against a 97% pass rate, an "onset" built from two failures) are
a separate PR.

### 1. A failure thrown by the test's own assertion had no failure window

The test asserts with
`expect(async () => expect(await variables.hasProgressBar()).toBe(true)).toPass()`. Every
`isVisible()` in that loop returned ok, so the trace had no errored call,
`findFailureWindow` returned null, and the log excerpt fell back to an error-line grep.
Its first line even blamed the wrong thing; the trace clock was fine:

```
(no trace clock available -- falling back to an error-line grep, which cannot show info-level evidence or silence)
```

`findFailureWindow` now anchors on the failure screenshot that `reporting.fixtures.ts`
takes the instant the test function throws, before afterEach runs: a `Page.screenshot`
with no `path`. A test's own `takeScreenshot` always passes a path, and the match is on
the Page class because tests take pathless *locator* screenshots as buffers to compare
(plots, notebook outputs). The failing action is whatever ended right before that
screenshot:

- **An errored call: the last one before the screenshot, not the first.** A `toPass` or a
  page object's own retry logs every attempt it catches as an errored call. In positron
  run [37477123593](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/actions/runs/37477123593)'s
  `Python - Install, search, and uninstall package`, the first errored call was a caught
  quick-input retry 98 s before the packages-list `expect` that actually failed the test,
  which ended 8 ms before the screenshot.
- **Else a retry loop** of 3 or more identical read calls. Here it was 8 `isVisible` calls
  on `.variables-core .monaco-progress-container`, which is exactly the 5 s `toPass` window.
- **Else the screenshot alone**, as the deadline.

Without the screenshot (a passing retry), behavior is unchanged: the first errored call,
or null. An inferred window says so in both the console digest and the log excerpt.

The console digest now focuses on that window too. With no errored call it had shown 15
app-startup lines, which the analyzer read as "cut off before the failing action". Its
30 s look-back also now runs from when the wait began rather than from the deadline, so
a 60 s `expect` still shows the command that started it.

The DOM-presence check now uses the failing action's own selectors, carried on the
window. It had used the selectors of every errored call, so the Python test's report
listed the caught quick-input retries' tokens against the packages-list wait. It also had
nothing for a test-thrown failure, and now gets the retry loop's selector. For this run
that adds the line the analyzer was missing: `monaco-progress-container` rendered for
session 1 but was NEVER in the DOM during the failing wait.

When a window has no known start (the screenshot alone), lines up to the deadline are
tagged `[before deadline]` rather than `[during wait]`, since nothing established when
the wait began.

Errored calls are also now paired with their own `before` by `callId`. Calls overlap, and
in that same Python trace the nearest preceding `before` belonged to a different call.

### 2. Kernel send order never reached the model

Even with a window, the kernel logs rank as bystanders for a variables test and get 8
lines, which in this run all went to heartbeats. The log miner now adds a **kernel
messages** section from the `<Language> Supervisor` logs: every `>>> SEND` (an
execute_request with its code, a comm_msg with its comm and method) and each execute or
lifecycle state change, tagged against the wait like the console digest. For this run:

```
15:19:52.138 [before action] r-fa94cab0 SEND execute_request code="hello <- 1; foo <- 2"
15:19:52.249 [before action] r-fa94cab0 SEND comm_open target=positron.lsp
15:19:53.003 [before action] r-fa94cab0 SEND comm_msg positron-variables-r-3-aab2aa02 method=clear
15:19:53.076 [during wait] r-fa94cab0 SEND execute_request code="Sys.sleep(20)"
15:19:53.077 [during wait] r-fa94cab0 State idle => busy (execute_request)
```

The busy/idle flip around every comm and info request, and `comm_info_request` itself,
are dropped as noise. The section has its own 40-line budget. Over budget it drops
post-deadline lines, then the earliest lines before the action, and with no known start it
keeps the latest lines, nearest the failure.

### 3. No screenshots since the Playwright 1.63 bump

Trace format v9 (#16103, Sep 16) moved screencast frames from a `sha1` file name under
`resources/` to `file: "screencast/..."`. Every frame read as `sha1=undefined`, so **every
analysis since then has had zero screenshots**: this run, and the last six analyzer runs
on main that I checked. It also dropped the timeline's `Trace t=0` line, which reads the
same field. Frames are now read from either shape.

Frames are also now taken at or before the failure screenshot rather than from the end of
the trace. The trace's last frames showed afterEach's layout reset, not the failure.
Without a failure screenshot the trace's last frames are kept, since the first errored
call is then often a caught retry, not the failure. The new last
frame for this test shows Variables already reading "No variables have been created"
while `Sys.sleep(20)` is still running in the console: the race, visible in one frame.

### 4. Submodule bumps were one opaque path

The positron-builds head commit was a dependabot bump whose only changed file is
`positron`. With nothing else to go on, the analyzer wrote that the range "plausibly
touches variables/session-switching code". `e2e-gather-run-info.js` now expands each
gitlink bump into its commits and files with the compare API, and the prompt lists them.
Here that is 4 commits (Quarto CRLF, CI triage, Windows pak, Snowflake), none in
variables. If the range can't be fetched, the prompt says the change set is unknown
rather than leaving a gap to guess into.

The compare API lists only commits ahead of the base, so a downgrade (status `behind`)
would have read as "0 commits" -- no change -- when commits were removed. A bump with
`behind_by > 0` now also fetches the reverse range and lists the removed commits and
files. Checked against the real API by reversing this run's bump: the forward range has
0 commits and 0 files, and the 4 commits now show as REMOVED.

### Validation

- Unit tests: 155 pass, with new cases built from the two traces above:
  `node --test ".claude/skills/e2e-failure-analyzer/scripts/test/*.test.js" ".claude/skills/debug-e2e-test/scripts/test/*.test.js"`
- `e2e-process-s3.js` against this run's report: 3 frames per attempt (was 0), the
  inferred window, the DOM-presence line above, and the kernel section above.
- `e2e-process-project.js` (blob path) against positron run 37477123593: 3 frames per
  attempt (was 0). The Python test's failing trace anchors on the packages-list `expect`,
  and its DOM presence lists only that call's tokens.
- `e2e-gather-run-info.js` against this run: the bump expands as above. `npm run precommit`
  is clean.

**What local checks cannot cover:** I did not re-run the model on the new evidence, so
this PR shows the evidence now reaches it, not that the verdict flips. The rubric PR is
the half that teaches it what to do with a send order that contradicts the test's step
order.

### Notes for review

- The failure-screenshot anchor relies on `reporting.fixtures.ts` capturing through
  Playwright's private `_onDidFinishTestFunctionCallbacks` hook. If an upgrade removes it,
  the fixture already falls back to capturing at teardown. The window then degrades to a
  later screenshot-only window; it doesn't break.
- A flaky test's log excerpt is still mined from its last attempt, which is the passing
  retry. The Action doesn't render excerpts for flaky tests, so I left that alone.
- `screenshotShas` / `lastScreenshotSha1` in the processed JSON are renamed to
  `screenshotFrames` (`{entry, timestamp}`) / `lastScreenshotEntry`, since v9 frames
  have no sha1. Nothing in-repo reads the old names; SKILL.md is updated.
- `buildConsoleDigest`, `selectorTokens` and `cleanConsole` were copy-pasted into all
  three trace scripts (only comments differed). They now live in `lib-failure-window.js`,
  `collectFailingSelectors` is replaced by the window's `selectors`, and each trace
  computes its failure window once. Only `parseTrace` itself is still duplicated.

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- N/A

#### Bug Fixes

- N/A

title: drive-positron: 1 helper fix from the nightly run
description:
### Summary

Nightly self-heal: 1 helper fixed, ready to review.

**To do:** Review and merge this PR.

#### terminal-run --read: fixed

- **What broke:** `terminal-run.sh --read` could not read a terminal's text on Linux; the Accessible View never opened.
- **Why:** It pressed Alt+F2, which the terminal passes to the shell instead of Positron.
- **Fix:** It opens the Accessible View from the Command Palette, keeping focus on the terminal.
- **Checked:** failed 3 of 3 tries before the fix; check.ts and the smoke terminal section pass with it (the next nightly runs all of smoke).

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

**Reason:** dp-terminal.ts read() pressed Alt+F2 on the focused xterm to open the Accessible View. In a terminal, a key reaches the workbench only if its command is in DEFAULT_COMMANDS_TO_SKIP_SHELL (upstream src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/common/terminal.ts, no Positron block; checked in terminalInstance.ts attachCustomKeyEventHandler, also upstream). editor.action.accessibleView is not in that list, so xterm sends Alt+F2 (and the Linux primary Shift+Alt+F2) to the shell: on the kept smoke instance both presses left the view closed and put a stray 'Q' on the bash prompt. The same command run from the Command Palette ('Open Accessible View', listed with keybinding Shift+Alt+F2) opened the view with smoke-42 in it. The fix opens it from the palette inside the page function (lib.openQuickInput + exact lib.pick + lib.clickRow, without paletteRun's blur, so focus returns to the terminal before the command runs), with the title in selectors.ts names.palette.openAccessibleView. Upstream cause, so the helper adapts; no smoke check changed. Not state-dependent: the case fails on its own group (--until, no --from-start).

**Tries:**
- smoke, fail: exit 1: {"ok":false,"index":1,"visible":1,"error":"the Accessible View did not open"}
- rerun, fail: exit 1: {"ok":false,"index":1,"visible":1,"error":"the Accessible View did not open"}
- fixer, fail: smoke --until 'terminal-run --read' --keep: FAIL with {"ok":false,"index":1,"visible":1,"error":"the Accessible View did not open"}; by hand on net1 the same; Alt+F2 and Shift+Alt+F2 on the focused xterm-helper-textarea left .accessible-view absent and typed 'Q' at the prompt; Command Palette 'Open ...

**To reproduce:**

```sh
node .claude/skills/drive-positron/test/smoke.ts --until "terminal-run --read"
terminal-run.sh --read --tail 5
```

**Commit:** fbc98e9da6bbb3ca4011bc3b9c7eb89d3d57cb19

</details>

title: Stop shipping upstream theme extensions hidden from the theme picker
description: Fixes #8162 Positron hides 8 upstream color themes from the theme picker: Abyss, Kimbie Dark, Monokai, Monokai Dimmed, Quiet Light, Red, Solarized Dark, and Solarized Light. However, our release builds still ship the 8 extensions that contain these themes. As a result, these extensions show in the Extensions view under `@builtin`, but you cannot select their themes. This PR removes the 8 extensions from release packaging. It adds them to the list of excluded extensions in `build/lib/extensions.ts` (desktop and web builds) and in `build/gulpfile.reh.ts` (server builds). The extension folders stay in the repository, so upstream merges do not get more conflicts: The picker filter in `positronColorThemeFilter.ts` keeps all of its entries. The 8 themes still load when you run Positron from sources, so the filter keeps the picker the same in dev builds and release builds. The filter is also necessary for the 6 hidden themes in `theme-defaults`, which continues to ship. **Behavior change:** Some users might have set one of these 8 themes in `workbench.colorTheme` by hand. For these users, Positron now uses the default Positron Dark or Positron Light theme. The picker never showed these themes, so this change affects only users who literally typed the theme name into `settings.json`. These users cannot install the themes again from Open VSX, because the themes are not published there. **Note for reviewers:** `product.json` still lists Solarized Dark and Solarized Light in `onboardingThemes`. Positron turns off the onboarding flow (`suppressOnboarding` in `startupPage.ts`), so I did not change this upstream block. ### Release Notes #### New Features - N/A #### Bug Fixes - Remove 8 upstream theme extensions that showed under `@builtin` in the Extensions view but had no themes that you can select (#8162) ### Validation Steps @:extensions Do these steps in a release build of this branch. A dev build still includes the 8 extensions. 1. Open the Extensions view and filter on `@builtin`. Make sure that the Themes section does not show Abyss, Kimbie Dark, Monokai, Monokai Dimmed, Quiet Light, Red, Solarized Dark, or Solarized Light. 2. Run _Preferences: Color Theme_. Make sure that the list of themes is the same as in the current release. 3. In `settings.json`, set `"workbench.colorTheme": "Monokai"`. Make sure that Positron uses the default dark theme and does not show an error.

title: Let extensions read, open and point at the user's data connections
description:
Part of the SQL editor work tracked by #15762. **PR 1 of 4** in a stack -- see [The stack](#the-stack) below.

### Summary

Opens the user's Data Connections to extensions. An extension can now list the connections the
user has configured, read one's schema, open one, and point the pane at a particular row.

The new `positron.dataConnections` API surface:

- `getConnections()` -- the user's saved and discovered connections
- `getSchema(profileId, options)` -- a bounded walk of a live connection's schema tree
- `onDidChangeConnections` -- fires when a connection opens or closes, or a profile changes
- a command to reveal a table, view or column in the Data Connections pane

There is no SQL anywhere in this PR. It is the platform the three PRs above it build on, and it
stands on its own: any extension that wants to know what the user is connected to can use it.

Two things worth a reviewer's attention:

**The schema walk is split from the summary.** `summarizeDataConnectionSchema` renders the schema
to compact lines for Assistant, which is the wrong shape for an extension that navigates the tree
(a SQL editor resolving a table to its columns would have to parse the lines back). The walk is now
exported separately as `walkDataConnectionSchema`, and `summarizeDataConnectionSchema` is a thin
renderer on top of it. Assistant's payload is unchanged -- it does not pay for a tree it cannot
read -- and the existing summary tests are untouched.

**The view id moved to the service's interfaces.** The service opens its own view, and
`workbench/services/**` cannot import from `workbench/contrib/**` (there are zero such imports on
`main`). `POSITRON_DATA_CONNECTIONS_VIEW_ID` now lives in the service interfaces, and
`positronDataConnectionsConfiguration.ts` re-exports it so this layer's callers are unchanged. This
also removes the duplicate copy the driver manager was carrying for the same reason.

### The stack

The SQL editor feature was written as one branch and split into four PRs, each reviewed as the diff
against the one below it:

| # | Branch | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| **1** | **`sclark/sql-1-core-connections`** | **this PR** -- core + API only |
| 2 | `sclark/sql-2-analyzer` | the `sql-analyzer` crate, its wasm, and statement ranges |
| 3 | `sclark/sql-3-support` | completions, diagnostics, hover, links, dialects |
| 4 | `sclark/sql-4-core-sessions` | sessions, the driver extensions, and cmd+enter execution |

`SQL-STACK.md`, a temporary note recording which PR owns which file while the stack is open, lives
in the PRs above this one and is dropped before the last of them merges. This PR does not carry it.

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- Extensions can read, open and reveal the user's data connections through a new
  `positron.dataConnections` API (#15762)

#### Bug Fixes

- N/A

### Validation Steps

@:connections

No e2e tests are added: this PR adds an API surface with no user-visible UI of its own, and it is
covered by unit tests at the level the behavior lives (284 vitest tests across the data connections
service, the tree, and the ext host bridge). The tag above runs the existing Data Connections
suites as a regression check on the pane, which this PR touches.

To exercise the API by hand:

1. Open the Data Connections pane and connect to any database (DuckDB is easiest).
2. From an extension or the command palette's developer tools, call
   `positron.dataConnections.getConnections()` and confirm the connection is listed with its
   `profileId`.
3. Call `getSchema(profileId)` and confirm you get a node tree of catalogs, schemas, tables and
   columns -- not rendered text.
4. Run the reveal command with a `{profileId, path}` naming a table, and confirm the pane expands to
   that row, selects it, and scrolls it into view.
5. Confirm a path naming a table that no longer exists does nothing, rather than raising an error.

title: Data Apps: show each Python editor's own run app buttons in split editors
description:
Part of #15917: Python apps only, will tackle the Shiny side in separate PRs to posit-dev/shiny-vscode. Each Python editor's run and debug app buttons now reflect its own document, whichever editor is focused: * Shiny `app.R` no longer shows "Run Dash App in Terminal" * two Python apps side by side each keep their own button * plain script next to an app keeps "Run Python File in Console" The `pythonAppFramework` context key is replaced by `pythonAppResources` and `pythonAppResources.`, lists of document URIs matched with `resource in ...`. With a Dash app editor active, the same editor's button says Dash: With a Dash app editor active, a Python script's button does not say Dash: ### Release Notes #### New Features - N/A #### Bug Fixes - Run and debug app buttons now match each editor's own Python app when several editors are open side by side (#15917) ### Validation Steps @:apps
Setup Run this in a Positron terminal, from wherever you keep scratch work: ```bash bash -euo pipefail <<'SETUP' mkdir 15917-run-app-buttons cd 15917-run-app-buttons python3 -m uv venv .venv/bin/activate uv pip install dash flask cat > dash_app.py <<'PY' from dash import Dash, html app = Dash(__name__) app.layout = html.Div("Hello Dash") if __name__ == "__main__": app.run() PY cat > flask_app.py <<'PY' from flask import Flask app = Flask(__name__) @app.route("/") def hello(): return "Hello Flask" PY cat > script.py <<'PY' print("just a script") PY cat > app.R <<'R' library(shiny) shinyApp(fluidPage("Hello Shiny"), function(input, output, session) {}) R SETUP ``` Open `15917-run-app-buttons` as the workspace and select `15917-run-app-buttons/.venv` as the Python interpreter. ---
1. Open `dash_app.py`, then open `app.R` to the side (right-click in the Explorer > Open to the Side). 2. Click into `dash_app.py`. The `app.R` editor's run button and its dropdown show only R actions, not "Run Dash App in Terminal". 3. Replace `app.R` in the right group with `flask_app.py` and click into it. The left editor's run button still reads "Run Dash App in Terminal" and the right one "Run Flask App in Terminal". Click into `dash_app.py`; neither changes. 4. Replace `flask_app.py` with `script.py` and click into `dash_app.py`. The `script.py` editor's run button reads "Run Python File in Console". 5. Add `import streamlit` to `script.py`. Within a second its button changes to "Run Streamlit App in Terminal"; undo the edit and it changes back. 6. Click the "Run Dash App in Terminal" button in the unfocused left editor. The Dash app starts and previews in the Viewer. With `app.R` focused, the Python editor still shows "Run Shiny App" - that is the Shiny extension, not covered here.

title: Scale Quarto inline output and Data Explorer grid with editor font size
description: Closes #16391 Inline output in Quarto documents now scales with `editor.fontSize`. Before this change, the output text grew with the editor font, but the spacing and the inline Data Explorer grid stayed at fixed pixel sizes. At large font sizes, tables looked cramped and text overflowed the grid cells. Now, they look much nicer: Or teeny tiny: ### Summary - **Inline output spacing.** The padding, margins, and gaps in `quartoOutputViewZone.css` now use `em` units. The values match the old pixel design at a 12px editor font, so the default look on macOS does not change. The space for the close button stays at a fixed 32px, because that button does not scale. - **Inline Data Explorer grid.** The new `inlineGridMetrics.ts` calculates the row height, header height, column width, and cell padding from the editor font size and line height. At the default font size, these values are the same as the old fixed values. The row height is never less than the editor line height plus padding, so a large `editor.lineHeight` does not make rows overlap. When the font size or line height changes, Positron rebuilds the grid. This change also applies to the inline Data Explorer in Positron notebooks. - **Data Explorer header.** In Quarto, the header and status messages now use the workbench font, the same as the full Data Explorer. Only the grid cells use the editor font. - **View zone height.** The height calculation now reads the em-based margins from the computed style and rounds the result up to a whole pixel. I did not change anything about how a language-specific font size, for example `"[quarto]": { "editor.fontSize": 20 }`, scales the HTML output but not the inline Data Explorer grid. The grid reads the global `editor` settings. A fix for that needs a change to the shared data grid font code, so it is not part of this PR. ### Release Notes #### New Features - N/A #### Bug Fixes - Quarto inline output, including HTML tables and the inline Data Explorer, now scales with the editor font size (#16391) ### Validation Steps @:quarto @:positron-notebooks @:data-explorer 1. Open a `.qmd` file. Run a cell that shows an HTML table, for example `knitr::kable(head(mtcars))`. 2. Run a cell that returns a data frame, so that the inline Data Explorer shows. 3. Set `editor.fontSize` to 28. Make sure that the table padding and the grid rows, headers, and columns grow with the text. 4. Set `editor.fontSize` to 8. Make sure that the output text does not go under the close button. 5. Set `editor.lineHeight` to 40. Make sure that the grid rows do not overlap. 6. Restart the kernel, so that the inline Data Explorer shows "disconnected". Then change `editor.fontSize`. Make sure that the "disconnected" message stays. 7. Open a Positron notebook with an inline Data Explorer. Do step 3 again.

title: Fix scroll wheel in dynamic modal dialogs on Positron Web
description:
Addresses #16441

### Summary

On Positron Web, the mouse wheel and trackpad did nothing in the content area of `PositronDynamicModalDialog`. The bug showed up in the **Add Data Connection** dialog, whose provider list could not be scrolled. Electron was not affected.

The cause is the web-only `BrowserWindow` (`src/vs/workbench/browser/window.ts`). It calls `preventDefault()` on every wheel event that reaches the workbench container, to block macOS back/forward swipe gestures. Modal overlays are rendered inside that container, so this also cancels native `overflow: auto` scrolling in the dialog.

This PR stops wheel propagation at the dialog box, so the events never reach that listener. The notebook component and the older connections modal already use the same workaround. The fix is in the shared dialog component, so every dynamic modal now scrolls on web.

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- N/A

#### Bug Fixes

- Fixed mouse wheel scrolling in the Add Data Connection dialog on Positron Web (#16441)

### QA Notes

@:web

1. Open Positron Web.
2. Open the **Add Data Connection** dialog.
3. Hover over the provider list and scroll with the mouse wheel or trackpad. The list should scroll.
4. Repeat in the Electron build to confirm scrolling still works there.

title: Add new screenshot for Data Connections docs page
description: Addresses #15378 ### Summary This PR adds a release screenshot for the new Data Connections docs page. The spec makes `data-connections.png`, which the nightly and publish runs of the Release Screenshots workflow will then keep up to date: The screenshot shows the `order_tracking.duckdb` test database in the Data Connections view. The spec expands the tables and views in the tree. It selects the `v_product_sales` view and expands it to show its columns. It also opens this view in the Data Explorer and expands the `units_sold` column profile in the summary panel. Some notes on the spec: - The view has no `ORDER BY`, so the spec sorts by `gross_revenue`. Without a sort, the row order changes from run to run and the nightly compare flags the image as changed. The `gross_revenue` column has no ties except at 0. - The spec sets `SNOWFLAKE_HOME` to an empty path for the app. A `connections.toml` file on the test machine then cannot add a "Detected" row to the tree. - The capture has no baked-in drop shadow. The docs page adds the shadow with the `{.drop-shadow}` class, the same as `data-explorer.png`. This PR also adds a shared `hideApiTestsStatusBar` helper and calls it from `prepareForScreenshot`. Builds from source load the upstream `vscode-api-tests` extension, which adds a "Hello" item to the status bar. Release builds do not include this extension. The helper hides the item, so local runs and `build_from_source` runs match release-build runs for all specs. The docs page change and the first copy of the image go in a separate PR over at `posit-dev/positron-website`. ### Release Notes #### New Features - N/A #### Bug Fixes - N/A ### Validation Steps @:connections This PR changes only the release screenshots project, which no e2e tag runs. To check the screenshot, run the spec locally: ```bash npx playwright test test/e2e/release-screenshots/data-connections/data-connections.screenshot.ts --project release-screenshots ``` Then look at `test/e2e/release-screenshots/output/data-connections.png`. You can also start the Release Screenshots workflow on this branch in nightly mode with "Build Positron from source" selected.

title: e2e: de-flake DuckDB viewConnection on macOS and wait for Workbench before Foundry managed credentials
description:
Fixes the two test failures in positron-builds nightly run [37295338161](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron-builds/actions/runs/37295338161) (2026.10.0-226). Neither is a regression from that build; both have prior history.

### Summary

**DuckDB connection test on macOS (failed both attempts; 4 occurrences on mac since Sep 25, 100% elsewhere).** `viewConnection()` checked the pane's two states sequentially: 5s for the details view, then a 30s click on the connect icon in the list. The pane itself swaps the list for the details view on the kernel's focus event after its own up-to-5s registration poll ([positronConnections.tsx:52](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/contrib/positronConnections/browser/positronConnections.tsx#L52)). On a slow mac runner that swap lands after the test's 5s window, unmounting the list item the test is now waiting on, so the click times out even though the pane is already where the test wants it. `viewConnection()` now polls both states in one `toPass` loop with a short click timeout, so a late swap is seen on the next iteration instead of hanging. The DuckDB test also waits for the console execution to finish before focusing the pane. Other callers (Postgres, SQLite, the screenshot tests) want the same end state and are unaffected.

**Foundry "model responds" test on the Azure Workbench lane (failed both attempts; same failure on Oct 1, passed Sep 28, Sep 30, Oct 2).** The overflow menu opened with no "Model" submenu for the whole budget, then the sibling Foundry test passed 13.5s later in the same worker. `hasManagedCredentials()` reports Foundry managed credentials as absent until `rstudio.rstudio-workbench` is active, and both that extension and the authentication extension activate on `onStartupFinished`, so the order is not fixed. When the assistant asks for the `ms-foundry` session first, it gets none and no models, and nothing re-fires the session unless the Workbench provider happens to emit a session change later. This is the first-attempt cause that #16358 left as a follow-up. `registerFoundryProvider()` now awaits the Workbench extension's activation when it is not yet active, then re-seeds the endpoint and fires `ms-foundry` sessions-changed so consumers re-query. The endpoint seeding moved into `seedFoundryEndpoint()` so it can run on both paths.

The Ubuntu electron lane in the same run was cancelled at its 120-minute job timeout with no failing test; that is a positron-builds workflow matter and is not addressed here.

### Release Notes

#### New Features
- N/A

#### Bug Fixes
- Microsoft Foundry managed credentials on Posit Workbench are now picked up when the Workbench extension activates after the authentication extension, instead of leaving Posit Assistant with no Foundry models until a later session change.

1. The connections suite should pass on all desktop lanes, including macOS.
2. The Azure shard of the Workbench lanes (current and last-stable Workbench, the latter being the nightly lane that failed) runs both Foundry tests; both should pass on the first attempt. The attached `logs-posit-assistant-foundry.test.ts.zip` should show the Microsoft Foundry provider resolving the Workbench-managed session without a prior "absent" result once the Workbench extension activates.

title: 14653 data connections build catalog explorer view for snowflake
description:
Part of #14653

### Summary

This PR builds out the Snowflake catalog explorer in the Data Connections pane. Every object in the tree now has details, stages can be browsed as folders and files, and any object's name or fully qualified path can be copied. It builds on the node details editor added for semantic views in #16308. Filter, search, and sort, and Databricks parity, are left for follow-up PRs under #14653.

**Details for every Snowflake object.** Clicking a database, schema, table, view, stage, or stage file opens its details in preview mode; double-clicking a node whose details are all it has pins them. Databases and schemas show their path, kind, owner, creation time, origin, options, retention, and comment. Tables add row count, size, clustering, change tracking, and a Columns tab. Views add their secure and materialized flags, a Columns tab, and a Definition tab. Stages show their type, URL, cloud, directory table, credentials and encryption, and a Properties tab from `DESCRIBE STAGE`. Files show their path, size, last modification, and MD5. The tree now runs full `SHOW DATABASES`/`SCHEMAS`/`TABLES`/`VIEWS` in place of `SHOW TERSE` and keeps each row on its node, so most details cost no extra query. Like the rest of the tree, none of this needs a warehouse.

**Stage browsing.** Stages expand into folders and files built from `LIST`, and each folder lists its own prefix when expanded, so what it shows is current and Refresh works at any level. A listing reads at most 10,000 rows, streamed from the result rather than fetched whole, and says so when it was cut short. A stage the role can see but not read shows why instead of failing the expand. Connection problems still fail the expand, so the tree reports them.

**Copy Name and Copy Path.** Every node except groups offers Copy Name. Nodes with a path also offer Copy Path, which copies the quoted form that pastes straight into SQL, such as `"DB"."SCHEMA"."TABLE"` or `@"DB"."SCHEMA"."STAGE"/folder/file.csv`.

**Opening data.** Double-clicking a table, view, or column still opens it in the Data Explorer. A semantic view's logical table, whose data belongs to its base table, keeps its details instead. The details editor gains an Open in Data Explorer button. The pane's tree finds the node from its recorded path without expanding anything, reconnecting if need be. If the button had to open the connection, it hands that connection to the Data Explorer to close with it.

**For reviewers: API and shared code**
- `positron.d.ts`: `DataConnectionNode.path`, `DataConnectionNode.defaultAction`, and `DataConnectionNodeKind.Notice`, used for in-tree notes such as a cut-short listing.
- `IPositronDataConnectionsService`: `registerNodeOpener`, `hasNodeOpener`, and `openNodeInDataExplorer`. The pane's tree registers itself as the opener. A details editor opens the pane only when no tree exists yet, and the service waits briefly for one.
- `PositronTreeInstance.loadChildren(id)` loads a node's children without expanding it. Reveals and the opener now share one lookup for recorded paths, built on it.
- `SnowflakeClient.queryCapped` streams a result, reads at most N rows, and reports the total.
- `fileSize.ts` is now an identical copy in the Databricks and Snowflake drivers, with a guard test that keeps the copies in step.
- `group-stages` joins `CONTAINER_ONLY_KINDS`, so the Stages group no longer uses up a level of the AI schema summary.

**Verified live** against a Snowflake account:
- details for every object kind, including an imported share and a personal database;
- stage listing with nested folders, a folder name with a space, and a quoted stage name containing `/`;
- Copy Path values;
- the double-click rules;
- Open in Data Explorer with the pane hidden and with the connection closed.

Not verified live, but covered by unit tests: external stages, the 10,000-file cap, and the notice for a stage the role can't read.

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- The Data Connections pane shows details for Snowflake databases, schemas, tables, views, stages, and stage files (#14653)
- Snowflake stages can be browsed as folders and files (#14653)
- Data connection nodes offer Copy Name, and Copy Path where they have a path (#14653)
- Node details editors offer Open in Data Explorer for nodes that can be previewed (#14653)

#### Bug Fixes

- N/A

### Validation Steps

@:connections @:data-explorer

1. Connect to Snowflake and expand down to a schema with tables, views, and a stage. Click a database, a schema, a table, a view, and a stage, and check each details tab: Overview, Columns, Definition, and Properties.
2. Expand a stage with nested files. Check its folders, files, and sizes, and click a file to see its details. Add a file to a folder and Refresh that folder.
3. Right-click a table and a stage file, choose Copy Path, and paste the result into a query or a `LIST` in a worksheet.
4. Double-click a table: it opens in the Data Explorer. Double-click a semantic view's logical table: its details are pinned instead.
5. With a table's details open, switch the sidebar to the Explorer and press Open in Data Explorer. The data opens and the sidebar and tree stay as they were. Collapse the connection first to see it reconnect, then close the Data Explorer and see the connection close.

title: Bump `js-yaml` in `positron-r` lockfile for security
description:
This PR updates `package-lock.json` in `positron-r` to remove the high `js-yaml` advisories in this extension. The change is only in the lockfile, with no changes to `package.json`. The new version is inside the semver range that `mocha` already declares. This PR is part of the work for posit-dev/positron-builds#1269.

### Summary

I ran `npm audit fix --package-lock-only`. The change is:

- `js-yaml` 4.1.0 to 4.3.2. This removes three high advisories for quadratic CPU use: GHSA-52cp-r559-cp3m (merge-key chains), GHSA-5p4m-2wfm-xmqj (`!!omap` resolution), and GHSA-2883-xcg3-v3hh (empty merge sources). `js-yaml` comes through `mocha`, which is a dev dependency only. The extension does not ship it.

One high advisory is still open, for `serialize-javascript` through `mocha` 11. The audit also reports a moderate advisory for `mocha` and a low advisory for `diff`, from the same `mocha` dependency tree. To remove these advisories, we must move to `mocha` 12. That is a major version change, so it is not in this PR.

| Scope | Low | Moderate | High | Critical |

| All dependencies, before | 1 | 1 | 2 | 0 |
| All dependencies, after | 1 | 1 | 1 | 0 |

title: e2e: anchor R breakpoint gutter click on line number, not DOM order
description:
### Summary Fixes a Windows flake (8.3% on main) in "R - Verify session switching preserves breakpoint state". The breakpoint was set on the wrong line, so it never verified. - `setUnverifiedBreakpointOnLine` clicked `.margin-view-overlays>:nth-child(N)`, assuming DOM order matches line number - Monaco appends newly rendered margin rows after existing ones, so once the editor scrolls the Nth row can be another line (in CI it hit line 7, a comment) - The click now targets the gutter row whose line-number label is N - It first goes to line N, since the editor can reopen scrolled to the end of the file with line N not rendered - `setBreakpointOnLine` is unchanged: notebook cells hide line numbers by default ### Release Notes #### New Features - N/A #### Bug Fixes - N/A ### Validation Steps @:win @:debug @:ark R Breakpoints group passed 18/18 locally on electron (`--repeat-each 3`) with each commit; the Windows trigger wasn't reproducible on macOS. ### E2E Triage Diagnosis
🟢 High confidence -- Test bug: Debug POM clicks `.margin-view-overlays>:nth-child(N)` assuming DOM order == line number; Monaco appends newly rendered lines after the last child, so after the editor scrolls up the Nth child is a different line. The breakpoint lands on comment line 7, never verifies, and expectBreakpointVerified at spec line 364 times out after 30s. - **Test:** [R Breakpoints > R - Verify session switching preserves breakpoint state](https://connect.posit.it/e2e-test-insights/?tab=test_health&repo=positron&test=R%20Breakpoints%20%3E%20R%20-%20Verify%20session%20switching%20preserves%20breakpoint%20state%7C%7C%7Ctest%2Fe2e%2Ftests%2Fdebug%2Fr-debug.test.ts) - **Targeted failure:** Pattern A: expect(locator('.monaco-editor .codicon-debug-breakpoint').first()).toBeVisible() 30s timeout, win/electron, 8.3% on main - **Signal:** Error-context snapshot: Breakpoints view 'breakpoint_test.r 7, Unverified Breakpoint' and live region 'Added breakpoint, line 7'; timeline shows click on .margin-view-overlays>:nth-child(3), then the 30s wait, with no sessions.start/select reached; viewLayer.ts:523 inserts new line nodes with lastChild.insertAdjacentHTML('afterend'). - **Frequency:** 40/482 runs (8.3%) on main, win/electron - **Hypothesis:** The editor opens scrolled down (lines 5..11 rendered), then scrolls to the top, so lines 1..4 are appended after them. DOM order becomes 5,6,7,...,1,2,3,4 and nth-child(3) is line 7. Ruled out: a session-switch/DAP race (the switch is never reached) and ark failing to verify a valid line (the breakpoint is on a comment line). Unconfirmed: why the editor starts scrolled (inferred to be restored view state or layout after the prior dirty-document test).

title: Enrich Assistant's interpreter skill & add a runtime registration helper
description: Fixes #15450 Partially addresses #15587 (the Conda and Pixi part; environment modules still need separate work) ### Summary This lets Positron Assistant answer the main questions about interpreters: what's installed, which interpreter a project uses, how to install one, why an installed interpreter isn't showing up, and how to make it show up. To support these changes, there's a new command, Register Interpreter from Path, that the assistant (or a user) can run with a language and a path. Positron hands the path to that language's extension. The extension either registers the interpreter and saves the path in its settings so it stays available, or fails with a plain reason like "unsupported version" or "excluded by settings". That reason answers "why can't I see it". The work is done through a new optional hook on the runtime manager API, so any language extension can support it. R and Python both implement it using their existing checks. The registered interpreters list now also marks which interpreter the current workspace uses, so the assistant can answer "which interpreter does this project use". R now recognizes Conda and Pixi environments from the location of the R binary. Before, an R named only by its path (through the default interpreter, override, or custom binaries settings, or the new command) started without its environment activated, so its libraries and compilers were missing. It now gets the same activation as an R found by Conda or Pixi discovery. This also means a Conda R found on the PATH gets activated. Environment modules aren't covered, because one binary can belong to several module environments and the path alone can't say which one. We'll have to tackle that in #15587. The interpreters reference in the positron-commands skill has been updated with these commands and a step-by-step flow for interpreters that aren't showing up. ### Release Notes #### New Features - Positron Assistant can now explain why an installed interpreter isn't showing up and make it available, and can tell which interpreter a project uses (#15450) #### Bug Fixes - R interpreters in Conda or Pixi environments that are specified by path now start with their environment activated (#15587) ### Validation Steps @:interpreter @:sessions 1. Install an R or Python interpreter somewhere Positron doesn't scan by default. Ask Assistant why it isn't showing up. It should rescan, then register it by path, and the interpreter should appear in the interpreter picker. Reload the window and check it's still there. 2. Ask Assistant to register an interpreter Positron can't use, such as an R older than the minimum version or a path listed in the exclude setting. It should explain why. 3. Create a Conda environment with R and set the R default interpreter setting to that environment's R. Start a console and check that the Conda environment is active (for example, `Sys.getenv("CONDA_PREFIX")` is set). 4. Open a folder that has a running interpreter and ask Assistant which interpreter the project uses.

title: e2e: unskip the four window-reload tests
description:
Trial run for the reload-dependent skips from the e2e skip audit (follow-up to #16334, #16348 and #16372). Related: #16002.

### Summary

Four tests were skipped because `hotKeys.reloadWindow` was unreliable on Windows: the CDP session for the reloaded renderer goes mute for about 25 s (#16002). #16001 raised the post-reload workbench budget from 30 s to 60 s to tolerate that, so this PR removes the skips and lets CI decide.

- `lsp/lsp-outline.test.ts`: outline after reload with Python in the foreground, and with R in the foreground. Skipped in #11265 with no issue. These only run in the pyrefly lane.
- `notebooks-positron/notebook-scroll-position.test.ts`: scroll position restored after window reload. Skipped in #13853 with the comment "reloadWindow is unreliable".
- `sessions/session-mgmt.test.ts`: session, console, variables and plots persist after reload. Skipped in #7514 and annotated with #6843. The annotation is kept for this trial; if CI is green it can go in review, since #6843 is now about a React state-update pattern that #7993 addressed for this case.

All four pass 3/3 locally on macOS electron with one worker (R 4.5.3, Python 3.10.12).

Note that the session-mgmt test inherits the critical tag from its suite, so once merged it runs on every PR. If it is flaky in the Windows lane here, the plan is to narrow it to `test.skip(process.platform === 'win32', ...)` annotated with #16002 rather than skip it everywhere.

### First CI round (run 37056954544, commit f097707139)

Pyrefly, electron, unit and ext-host green; both outline reload tests passed first try in the pyrefly lane, and the scroll-position reload test passed on every lane including Windows. So the reload stall itself did not reproduce.

The session-mgmt reload test failed on chromium and Windows, both attempts, at the first `expectPlotThumbnailsCountToBe(2)` before the reload. Diagnosis:

- **Mechanism:** the Plots pane shares one sidebar column with Variables in this test. The automatic history policy in `positronPlots.tsx` hides the thumbnail strip when the pane is under 300 px wide or tall. The browser harness pins the viewport to 1200x800 and the Windows runner window is small; electron on Linux gets a full-size window and passed.
- **Evidence:** the DOM snapshot at the failure shows the matplotlib plot rendered, "Show Previous Plot" enabled (so both plots exist), no thumbnail strip, and an overflow button in the Plots toolbar. The electron lane and three local electron repeats passed the same assertion.
- **Ruled out:** the reload stall (#16002) and sessions not restoring (#6843), because the failure precedes the reload. A missing plot, because the snapshot shows it.
- **Fix:** removed the two pre-reload thumbnail counts (second commit). They were incidental; the post-reload ones were already commented out for #6036, `waitForCurrentPlot` proves each plot rendered, and plots.test.ts covers the history count on web. Green 3/3 locally on the chromium project after the change.

title: Owned runtime sessions and agent sessions (experimental)
description:
First step toward #14780. This PR introduces the concept of runtime session ownership, and its first user "agent sessions" which currently don't do anything other than rendering with a sparkle icon. We'll build on the new `owner` property in followups.

#### `RuntimeSessionMetadata.owner`

There can be two owners: `'user'` or `'agent'`. The owner is stored on the session metadata and persists across restore.

We don't do much for `agent` sessions yet. They use a sparkle icon instead of the language icon. We'll build on that in followup PRs.

Adds a new experimental setting `ai.agentSessions.enabled`. When enabled, the console's session menu gains "Start Agent Console Session..." (also in the command palette). When disabled, both are hidden.

Extensions can start an agent session via `positron.runtime.startLanguageRuntime(..., { owner: 'agent' })`. Core records the owner as given; Posit Assistant should check the setting before calling this. `owner` is optional on the public RuntimeSessionMetadata (absent means user), so existing runtime extensions are unaffected.

The setting only gates starting agent sessions. Existing ones keep their owner and icon if it's turned off, so they stay distinguishable from your own.

#### `startLanguageRuntime(..., { activate })` option

Also adds an independent `activate` option to `positron.runtime.startLanguageRuntime` (default `true`). Passing `activate: false` starts the session in the background and leaves the user's selected session in place. This is mainly to let agent create a session in the background without stealing the user's focus.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/834b2d3a-1d3a-4c22-a25d-43b3750d23a9

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- N/A

#### Bug Fixes

- N/A

### Validation Steps

@:console @:sessions

**Setting off (the default):**

1. Start a Python or R console.
2. Open the chevron next to "+" in the console title: there is no separator and no "Start Agent Console Session..." after "Start Another...".
3. The command palette does not list "Interpreter: Start Agent Console Session...".

**Setting enabled:**

1. Turn on `ai.agentSessions.enabled`.
2. The console "+" menu now ends with a separator and "Start Agent Console Session...", and the palette lists the command.
3. Click it. The interpreter quick pick opens, titled "Start Agent Console Session", with your foreground interpreter focused. Pick one.
4. A new console tab appears and takes the foreground, with a sparkle icon in place of the language glyph.
5. Open the session picker. The agent session's entry shows the same icon, aligned with the other icons.
6. Reload the window. The tab still shows the sparkle icon: the owner is on the persisted metadata.

title: python: support __file__ in console
description:
Fixes #6120

When Python code is run from a file in the editor, `__file__` is now set in the console's user namespace to that file's path. This matches how the code behaves when the file is run as a script, so patterns like `os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))` work.

The value stays set after the code runs. Code typed in the console afterwards, and functions defined in the file, can still use it. It only changes when code is run from another file on disk. Console input and editors not backed by a file (such as untitled buffers) leave any existing `__file__` alone. Like other module dunders, it is hidden from the Variables pane.

This reuses the file-path lookup already used to add the editor's directory to `sys.path`. That lookup is now its own `_get_editor_path` helper.

### Release Notes

#### New Features
- N/A

#### Bug Fixes
- Python: `__file__` is now defined when running code from a file in the editor (#6120)

### Validation Steps

@:console

1. Save a Python file, e.g. `~/scratch/script.py`, containing:

    ```python
    import os
    print(__file__)
    print(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
    ```

2. Run the file's lines in the console (Cmd/Ctrl+Enter, or Run Python File in Console).
3. Check that the file's full path and its directory are printed.
4. Type `__file__` in the console and check that it still shows the same path.
5. Run code from a second saved file and check that `__file__` now shows that file.
6. Run code from an untitled editor and check that `__file__` does not change.
7. Check that `__file__` does not appear in the Variables pane.

title: Retry Bedrock web-identity sign-in when the token file arrives late
description:
Addresses #15292

On Posit Workbench, the session agent writes the AWS web-identity token file (`AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE`) asynchronously. If the authentication extension activates first, the startup credential resolve fails with ENOENT. Nothing re-resolved the chain afterward, so the Bedrock provider stayed signed out for the whole session and every Assistant prompt failed with "No credentials available for provider: bedrock".

### Summary

- Moves the AWS credential chain into `createAwsCredentialChain` in `credentials/aws.ts` and adds a `shouldRefresh` hook. It retries a failed resolve once the token file exists, and again each time the file is rewritten. It does not re-resolve while credentials are held, because every STS exchange returns new credentials and would fire a `changed` event every few minutes. Expiring credentials still refresh through their expiration.
- Adds `watchWebIdentityTokenFile`, which polls the token file with `fs.watchFile` and calls `resolveChainCredentials()` when a retry is due. This fires the `added` session event, so consumers waiting for that event get credentials without calling `getSessions`. I used `fs.watchFile` instead of `createFileSystemWatcher` because the latter misses the file's creation when its parent folder does not exist yet.
- Adds `scripts/mock-aws-auth-server`, a dev-only stand-in for AWS STS (`npm run mock-aws-auth-server`, or the **Mock AWS Auth Server** task) for testing web-identity sign-in locally. It writes the token file on request (standing in for the Workbench session agent) and hands out fake credentials, or real ones (from an AWS CLI profile or env vars) so Bedrock works end to end.
- Fixes two related races where overlapping resolves conflict:
  - In `AuthProvider`, a stale failure that lands after a newer successful resolve no longer signs out the session that the newer resolve created.
  - In the AWS chain, a stale failure no longer clears the "credentials held" flag, so it does not turn token-file refreshes back on.
- One race is documented and accepted. If the token file appears between a resolve recording its mtime and reading the file, a second resolve can start. Both resolves succeed, so the user stays signed in, at the cost of one extra STS exchange.

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- N/A

#### Bug Fixes

- Fixed Posit Assistant sometimes failing with "No credentials available for provider: bedrock" when a Posit Workbench session started before its AWS identity token was available (#15292)

### Validation Steps

@:assistant

Unit coverage is in `extensions/authentication/src/test/aws.test.ts`:

```sh
npm run test-extension -- -l authentication
```

Manual check with the new mock AWS auth server (no Workbench needed). The full walkthrough is in `scripts/mock-aws-auth-server/README.md`.

1. Start the server with real credentials. The mock answers the SDK's token exchange with whatever credentials you give it, and those are what the extension uses to call Bedrock. Use an AWS CLI profile that has Bedrock access (run `aws sso login --profile <profile>` first if it is an SSO profile), either:

   - **By profile name.** The server fetches the profile's credentials on each exchange:

     ```sh
     npm run mock-aws-auth-server -- --profile <profile>
     ```

   - **Or as env vars.** The subshell keeps the exported `AWS_*` variables out of your shell:

     ```sh
     (
       eval "$(aws configure export-credentials --profile <profile> --format env)"
       MOCK_AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=$AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID \
       MOCK_AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=$AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY \
       MOCK_AWS_SESSION_TOKEN=$AWS_SESSION_TOKEN \
       MOCK_AWS_CREDENTIAL_EXPIRATION=$AWS_CREDENTIAL_EXPIRATION \
       npm run mock-aws-auth-server
     )
     ```

   The startup line should say `credentials from AWS profile <profile>` or `credentials from MOCK_AWS_* env vars`. With no credentials, the server hands out fake ones. That is enough for steps 2-6, but Bedrock rejects fake credentials, so models won't load.

   On startup the server removes any token file left by an earlier run, so Positron starts without one, as on Workbench before the session agent writes it.

2. In another terminal, launch Positron from sources with web-identity auth pointed at the server (the server prints these lines at startup):

   ```sh
   export AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE=/tmp/mock-aws-auth/id_token
   export AWS_ROLE_ARN=arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/bedrock
   export AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_STS=http://localhost:4599
   export AWS_REGION=us-east-1             # a region where the profile has Bedrock access
   unset AWS_PROFILE AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY AWS_SESSION_TOKEN
   export AWS_CONFIG_FILE=/dev/null AWS_SHARED_CREDENTIALS_FILE=/dev/null
   ./scripts/code.sh --log positron.authentication:debug
   ```

3. In the **Authentication** output channel, confirm an `[AWS]` credential resolution failed with `ENOENT ... id_token`.
4. Have the server write the token file, standing in for the Workbench session agent: `curl localhost:4599/token`
5. Within about 5 seconds, the server logs `AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity #1` and the channel logs `[AWS] Credential resolution resolved`, without a reload. With real credentials, Bedrock models load and an Assistant prompt using a Bedrock model succeeds.
6. Rewrite the token a few times with `curl localhost:4599/token`, more than 5 seconds apart. The server should log no new exchanges while credentials are held.
7. Optional, credential expiry: restart the server with `--duration 120` added, reload the window, and sign in with `curl localhost:4599/token`. Rotate the token once more with `curl localhost:4599/token`. After the credentials expire (the server logs the expiration time), send an Assistant prompt. The server logs `AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity #2` with the rotated token, and the prompt succeeds.

title: Don't flag local Python modules as missing packages in Quarto documents and notebooks
description: Fixes #15518 The missing-packages check flagged local Python modules in Quarto documents and notebooks as missing packages. For example, `notebooks/analysis.qmd` with `from utils import run` and a sibling `notebooks/utils.py` offered `pip install utils`, which installs an unrelated PyPI project. The fix for scripts in #14655 did not cover Quarto documents or notebooks. ### Summary - Quarto and notebook checks now send the document URI with the extracted code, as script checks already do. The Python runtime uses the URI to find import roots. The cache key now includes the URI, so the same code in two folders gets two separate results. - The Python runtime now uses each folder from the document up to its workspace folder as an import root. A module at the project root is local, even when the document is in a subfolder. An untitled document gets no extra roots. A file outside all workspace folders gets only its own folder. On web and remote, the workspace folder lookup uses the on-disk path, because the remote extension host sees its workspace folders as `file` URIs. - The `RuntimeMissingPackagesTarget` docs now say that a caller can send both `code` and `uri`. When a caller sends both, the runtime analyzes `code`, and `uri` only identifies the source document. Script checks have worked this way since #14655, and both built-in runtimes read `code` first. - A new kernel test shows that a local module in any import root (not only the first root) is importable. ### Known limits This change prefers to not offer an install when it is not sure. A module or folder with the same name, anywhere between the document and the workspace root, stops the offer. This occurs even when the module does not import at run time (for example, when `notebook.workingDirectory` points to a different folder). The cost is one `ModuleNotFoundError`, and the console can still offer the install from that error. To offer an unrelated PyPI package for a local name is, I am arguing here, a worse failure. I'll note also that the check always asks pypi.org if a package exists, but pip and uv install from the index that you configure. ### Release Notes #### New Features - N/A #### Bug Fixes - Positron no longer offers to install a PyPI package for a local Python module that a Quarto document or notebook imports (#15518) ### Validation Steps @:packages-pane @:win Make this folder and open it as the workspace folder: ``` project/ ├── config.py └── notebooks/ ├── analysis.qmd └── utils.py ``` Put this chunk in `analysis.qmd`: ```` ```{python} from utils import run import config ``` ```` 1. Start a Python console and open `notebooks/analysis.qmd`. Expected: no missing-packages badge. Before this change, the badge showed `utils`. 2. Set `quarto.inlineOutput.enabled` to `true`, reopen the file, and run the chunk to start the document session. Expected: no badge. 3. Add `import requests` (or another real package that is _not_ installed) and save. Expected: the badge shows only `requests`. 4. Copy `analysis.qmd` to a different folder that has no `utils.py`, and open the copy. Expected: the badge shows `utils`. 5. Put the same imports in a notebook in `notebooks/` with a Python kernel. Expected: no badge.

title: e2e: unskip plot zoom and console queue-input tests
description:
Third PR in the e2e skip audit (after #16334 and #16348). Two unconditional skips come back, the Posit Assistant MCP suite comes back on its owner's request, and four release-screenshot tests are deleted on their owner's request.

### Summary

**Plot zoom (Fit vs. 200%)**, skipped in #11479 as "screenshot behaving oddly". The real failure was in the page object: #12037 gave the zoom actions a `checked` state, so Monaco renders them as `menuitemcheckbox`, and `setThePlotZoom` was looking for `menuitem`. The trace DOM snapshot shows the open menu with "Fit" as a checkbox item. Fix: `menuItemType: 'menuitemcheckbox'` in `pages/plots.ts`. The first PR run then showed the original "oddly behaving screenshot": the Fit vs. 200% pixel diff read 1.36% against a 1.5% floor on both Linux lanes. The test now asserts on the image's rendered width, which the pane sets to 100% at Fit and to twice the natural width at 200%, so it must change and then change back. Green 3/3 locally.

**Console: queue user input while interpreter is starting**, skipped in #14545 as "very flaky, cannot be manually reproduced". The June 2026 failing runs are no longer retained, so there is nothing to file a bug against. Console submission was rewritten in #15078 after the skip, which is the plausible fix. Green 5/5 locally. If it flakes on this PR, that run is the evidence for an issue.

**Posit Assistant MCP suite**, skipped in #14027 "while investigating failures". Jon asked to unskip it and see how it goes. The first PR run failed on every lane: the assistant now flags `.positai/` as legacy config and shows a second `.bg-warning` banner, which made the tool-confirmation locator ambiguous. The test now writes `.posit/assistant/settings.json`, the current location, and the locator is scoped to the card's border class. Green locally.

**Notifications center left open** (`dialog-toasts.ts`): the assistant welcome-page test failed its sign-in on every lane once the MCP suite ran ahead of it in the same worker. `Toasts.waitForAppear` opened the notifications center to look for a toast and, when none arrived, threw before closing it, so the center sat over the provider modal and swallowed the Connect click. #16371 landed that fix on main while this PR was open; this branch merges it and carries no change of its own there.

title: Support ${workspaceFolder} in Python interpreter path settings
description:
Fixes #10389 for Python. The R half is #16351, and this PR matches its behavior.

### Summary

Python interpreter path settings now support `${workspaceFolder}`, so a project can point Positron at a Python inside it:

```json
{
  "python.interpreters.include": ["${workspaceFolder}/envs/project"],
  "python.defaultInterpreterPath": "${workspaceFolder}/envs/project/bin/python"
}
```

Before, these values failed the absolute-path check and were dropped with a `not absolute...ignoring` log line. For `defaultInterpreterPath`, Positron then recommended the user-level Python at startup instead of the project's.

**Settings covered:** `python.interpreters.include`, `.exclude`, `.override`, and Positron's startup read of `python.defaultInterpreterPath`.

**Behavior, same as R:**

- Only `${workspaceFolder}` is supported. In a multi-root workspace, it's the first folder.
- A path that uses any other `${...}` (including `${env:NAME}` or a misspelling), or uses `${workspaceFolder}` with no folder open, is ignored with a log line that says why. In a list, only that entry is dropped.
- An absolute path containing a literal `${` used to be accepted. It's now ignored as an unsupported variable.
- The discovery cache key hashes the resolved paths, so two projects with the same `${workspaceFolder}/...` text don't share a cache entry.

Upstream code still reads `python.defaultInterpreterPath` through `SystemVariables`, which is more lenient. This PR leaves it alone.

### Screenshots

- Happy path:


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/96c4308b-0329-436a-9881-cd225fa8b992


- Unsupported variables next to a good path:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2495f5bd-e40d-435a-add3-9148c9d08e84



- No folder open:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/57125fd8-7aa8-4445-bd06-6e23762ab4a2



- Startup picks the project's Python:


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a4f6abc5-47af-4c52-bfc6-148d7e8e4a97


### Release Notes

#### New Features

- Python interpreter path settings (`python.interpreters.include`, `.exclude`, `.override`, and `python.defaultInterpreterPath`) now support `${workspaceFolder}`, so a project can point at a Python installed inside it (#10389)

#### Bug Fixes

- N/A

### Validation Steps

@:interpreter @:sessions

For the manual check, you need a Python inside the project that discovery doesn't find on its own. A uv standalone Python works:

```
uv python install 3.12 --install-dir tools/pythons
```

uv only creates `python3`. Add a `python` link next to it in the `bin` folder.

1. In the folder's settings, set `"python.interpreters.include": ["${workspaceFolder}/tools/pythons/<dir>/bin/python"]`.
2. Run **Python: Print interpreter debug information to Output**. `interpreters.include` shows the full resolved path, and the interpreter picker lists the project's Python.
3. Add `${env:PROJECT_PYTHON}/bin/python` next to the good entry. The output shows an "unsupported variable" line for it, and the good entry still works.
4. In a window with no folder open, a user-level `${workspaceFolder}/...` entry logs "...but no folder is open...ignoring".
5. Startup: in a folder with no `.venv`, `.conda`, or `*/bin/python`, create an env at `envs/project`. Set `python.defaultInterpreterPath` to `${workspaceFolder}/envs/project/bin/python`, and add `${workspaceFolder}/envs/project` to `include` so discovery finds it.
