title: ci: install macOS e2e Python deps into pyenv by absolute path
description:
Fixes the macOS e2e lanes installing every Python test dependency into the runner image's Python 3.14 instead of the pyenv 3.10.10 the tests select. Reported by Julia Silge in Slack on 2026-09-28.

### Summary

The macOS e2e job ran `python -m pip install` through the pyenv shims from the repo root. Since #15386 the root `.python-version` pins 3.12, which this job never installs. pyenv's shim resolution skips the missing version and falls back to `system` silently, with exit 0 and nothing in the log, so `python` resolved to `/Library/Frameworks/Python.framework/Versions/3.14`. pandas and friends landed there, the 3.10.10 environment stayed empty, and the pandas-dependent suites (data explorer, connections) timed out in every full-suite run since 2026-08-19. The 2026-07-24 run on the same macos-26-arm64 image and pyenv version installed into pyenv, so this is not a runner-image change.

This ports the fix that positron-builds landed for the identical symptom in posit-dev/positron-builds#1167:

- Call the interpreters by absolute path (`~/.pyenv/versions/<ver>/bin/python`) so neither the shims nor `.python-version` are involved.
- Assert `sys.version` before installing so a wrong or missing interpreter fails the step loudly instead of quietly populating the wrong environment.
- Drop the `pyenv init` evals and the `pyenv global` flip to 3.11.0 in the ipykernel step. `pyenv global 3.10.10` stays so Positron's interpreter discovery still reports it as the default.

The Docker lanes install with pyenv at image build time outside any checkout, and Windows does not use pyenv, so the macOS run workflow is the only place with this pattern.

### Release Notes

#### New Features
- N/A

#### Bug Fixes
- N/A

### Validation Steps

CI-only change; the PR e2e jobs run on Linux and do not exercise it. Validated with a Test: Full Suite dispatch on this branch with only the macOS arm64 lane enabled (link in the PR comments once it finishes). Success criteria: the "Install Python dependencies" step prints `/Users/runner/.pyenv/versions/3.10.10/bin/python`, pip installs report that path, and the data explorer and connections suites pass.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Serve Quarto code cell language features from Positron by default
description:
- Fixes #12837
- Fixes #13907
- Fixes #14512
- Fixes #14540
- Fixes #15230

This PR turns on `quarto.embeddedLanguageFeatures.native` by default. 🎉🥳🙌 

Positron now serves the language features for R and Python code cells in Quarto and R Markdown documents from the virtual `quarto-cells` notebook. The Quarto extension (1.138.0, already pinned) stands down for R and Python when the setting is on.

The PR has four parts:

- **Default flip.** The setting defaults to `true`, and the helper reads "unset" as on. I also updated the description, but I did decide to keep the setting `experimental` for at least few daily builds. I think we'll take that tag off before the next release.
- **One outline tree.** Core no longer registers its own document symbol provider for Quarto documents. That provider added a second, flat "Quarto Code Cells" group, so every code symbol showed two times. The Quarto extension now builds the only tree. It nests the cell symbols under their chunk through the new command `positron.executeQuartoCellSymbolProvider`.
- **Stale outline fix.** The new E2E spec found a bug. On first open, the outline showed no code symbols until the first edit. The outline cache in `outlineModel.ts` is keyed on the version of the document and its own provider list. The language server for a cell registers after the first request, and that registration does not change the provider list of the Quarto document. As a result, the cache kept the empty first answer. For Quarto and R Markdown documents, the cache now also compares a snapshot of the full registry. Other documents, which can include notebook cells, keep the upstream cache behavior. Note that the change is in an upstream file, inside Positron markers.
- **Tests that tell the two paths apart.** `quarto-outline.test.ts` makes sure that the outline is one nested tree, with each code symbol one time. `quarto-no-vdoc.test.ts` exercises the outline, hover, _Format Document_, run cell, <kbd>Cmd+Enter</kbd>, and completions in an R and a Python document and makes sure that the Quarto log has no R or Python `[vdoc] Created` lines. With the setting off, this spec fails with 30+ vdoc lines. The Python outline case needs Pyrefly, so it runs only when `ALLOW_PYREFLY=true`; this PR adds the spec to the Pyrefly workflow.

### Behavior changes

- R and Python cells no longer make temporary `.vdoc.` files, so there's nothing that can slip into the Problems pane.
- `quarto.cells.hoverHelp.enabled` and `quarto.cells.signatureHelp.enabled` no longer turn off hover and signature help in R and Python chunks as our native providers do not read these settings. Maybe we should do that? Or maybe people can choose between either the new native treatment or being able to turn those features off?
- The extension still makes R and Python vdocs for `quarto.formatCell`, because that command is not gated yet.

To go back to the old path, set `"quarto.embeddedLanguageFeatures.native": false`.

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- Positron now serves completions, hover, diagnostics, outline, formatting, and more for R and Python code cells in Quarto and R Markdown documents. The Quarto extension does not make temporary virtual documents for these languages. To use the old behavior, set `quarto.embeddedLanguageFeatures.native` to `false`.

#### Bug Fixes

- The outline for Quarto and R Markdown documents no longer shows a second Quarto group or each code symbol two times (#13907, #15230).
- The outline for Quarto and R Markdown documents with many code chunks now updates quickly (#14512).

### Validation Steps

@:quarto @:outline @:pyrefly

1. Open a `.qmd` file with an R chunk while a console session runs.
2. Open the outline. Make sure that it shows one tree, with the symbols of each chunk nested under that chunk. There must be no "Quarto Code Cells" group.
3. Make sure that the symbols appear on first open, before you edit the document.
4. Do the same with a Python `.qmd` file.
5. Set `quarto.embeddedLanguageFeatures.native` to `false`. Make sure that completions still work and that the outline is still one tree.

title: Bundle `@databricks/sql` in the Databricks data driver and update file-count budgets
description:
Addresses #16025

This PR makes the Databricks data driver ship 15 files instead of 3,145. It also updates the file-count budgets to match.

**Bundle `@databricks/sql` in its own esbuild entry point.** The driver kept `@databricks/sql` external. As a result, the full production dependency closure of the SDK shipped in the `node_modules` of the extension. Now esbuild bundles the SDK into a second entry point, `dist/databricksSdk.js` (2.7 MB minified). A new `.vscodeignore` keeps `src/`, `out/`, `tsconfig.json`, and the build scripts out of the package.

The SDK stays behind the existing lazy load of the driver. `databricksClient.ts` imports `./databricksSdk.js` with a dynamic import on the first connection attempt. This file is a thin shim that re-exports the SDK. `./databricksSdk.js` stays external in `extension.js`, so the import stays a real deferred load. As a result, activation of the extension does not parse the SDK. esbuild runs with `legalComments: 'eof'`, so the license comments in the dependencies of the SDK stay in the minified bundle.

The esbuild comment said that the SDK "cannot bundle cleanly" because of dynamic requires and a runtime read of `package.json`. This is not true for the installed version, 2.0.0. All of its requires are static, and the driver version is a constant in `dist/version.js`. The only real constraints are two native modules:

- **`lz4-napi` stays external and ships.** It decompresses LZ4-compressed query results. It is a napi-rs package that selects a `.node` file for each platform at runtime, so it cannot go in the bundle. The SDK asks the server for compressed results only when `lz4-napi` loads. Without it, queries work, but the results are not compressed. It adds 7 files (768 KB).
- **The native kernel backend does not ship.** The SDK loads it only when a client sets the internal `useKernel` option. Positron does not set it. Its binary is 13 MB for each platform.

To ship only `lz4-napi`, `package.json` moves `@databricks/sql` to `devDependencies` and declares `lz4-napi` as the only runtime dependency. The extension stays in `extensionsWithNpmDeps`. The Npm packaging strategy then ships `lz4-napi` and the `@antoniomuso/lz4-napi-<platform>` package for the build target, with no change to the build code. In the lockfile, the only change is the `"dev": true` flag on the closure of the SDK.

| Extension | Files before | Files after |
|---|---|---|
| `positron-data-driver-databricks` | 3,145 | 15 |

**Budget changes** in `build/lib/positron-path-budget.ts`:

- Remove the `positron-data-driver-databricks` entry (15 files, less than the default budget of 100).
- Lower `EXTENSIONS_FILE_COUNT_BUDGET` from 28,000 to 24,500. The expected count is about 22,400.

This PR and #16234 (Snowflake) both change `EXTENSIONS_FILE_COUNT_BUDGET`. The second PR to merge must rebase and lower the budget to about 19,500.

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- N/A

#### Bug Fixes

- N/A

### Validation Steps

@:connections

The data-connections E2E suite tests the Databricks driver against a real backend. This suite loads the extensions from source with the full `node_modules`, so it cannot find a module that is missing from the packaged build. For this reason, I also did these checks:

- The bundle builds with zero esbuild warnings. The only requires in the bundle that are not Node built-ins are `lz4-napi`, the kernel loader, and the optional `encoding` require of node-fetch (in a try block).
- I copied `dist/` and `lz4-napi` to a directory with no other `node_modules`. From there, `DBSQLClient` constructs, and `connect` makes a real network request (a nonexistent host fails with `ENOTFOUND`, as expected).
- From the location of the bundle, `lz4-napi` resolves to the shipped `node_modules` and does a compression round trip. Without `lz4-napi`, the SDK does not ask for LZ4 results.
- The SDK loads in 63 ms from the bundle, and in 86 ms from `node_modules`. `dist/extension.js` (49 KB) contains no SDK code.
- `tsc` passes for the extension. The extension tests pass (97 tests, `npm run test-extension -- -l positron-data-driver-databricks`). The lazy-load test gets a real client through the new shim.
- The build tests pass: `cd build && node --test lib/test/positron-path-budget.test.ts lib/test/positron-check-path-lengths.test.ts`.

To test by hand in a packaged build (for example, made with `npm run gulp vscode`):

1. Open the Data Connections pane and connect to a Databricks workspace. Browse the catalogs, schemas, and tables.
2. Run a query that returns many rows. The query must complete with no `lz4-napi` warning in the extension host log.
3. Look at the `File counts:` lines in the build log. `positron-data-driver-databricks` must not have its own line, because it has less than 100 files. The total for `extensions/` must be about 22,400.

title: Remove unused eslint dev dependencies from Positron extensions
description:
This PR removes the unused `eslint@8` dev dependencies from 17 Positron extensions. It is a follow-up to #16236, which removed the unused `mocha`, and it is part of setting us up for posit-dev/positron-builds#1269.

### Summary

These extensions declare `eslint@8`, `@typescript-eslint/eslint-plugin`, and `@typescript-eslint/parser` in `devDependencies`. These packages came from the initial extension template in 2022, and nothing uses them now:

- The root `eslint` config (`eslint.config.js`) lints all of these extensions, through `build/filters.ts`. The pre-commit hook uses the same config.
- The `lint` script in each extension fails on `main`. `eslint@8` finds the root `eslint.config.js` and stops with `Invalid option '--ext'`. No CI workflow runs these scripts. Only `positron-python` has its own lint in CI, and this PR does not change it.

The changes are:

- **17 extensions:** I removed the three packages from `devDependencies`. `open-remote-wsl` also loses `eslint-plugin-jsdoc`.
- **Scripts:** I removed the `lint` script. In 14 extensions, `pretest` changes from `npm run compile && npm run lint` to `npm run compile`. `npm test` in these extensions failed at the lint step before this change.
- **Config files:** I removed the unused `.eslintrc.json` in `positron-r` and `open-remote-wsl`, and `.eslintignore` in `open-remote-wsl`. The root flat config does not read these files.

The lockfile changes remove only dev packages (84 to 145 packages for each extension). No versions change. There are no changes to runtime dependencies or to code that we ship.

npm audit results for these 17 extensions:

| Scope | Critical | High | Moderate | Low |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| All dependencies, before | 1 | 17 | 1 | 1 |
| All dependencies, after | 1 | 4 | 1 | 1 |

This removes 13 high advisories for `js-yaml`, `@typescript-eslint`, and `minimatch`. Eight extensions go from one or more high advisories to 0.

### Not in this PR

- `open-remote-ssh` has the same unused packages. I did not change it here, because #16229 changes its lockfile. A small follow-up can remove them after #16229 merges.
- `positron-r` still gets `js-yaml` through `mocha@11`. A separate lockfile-only PR will update it.
- `copilot` comes from upstream, and `positron-python` uses its own lint. This PR does not change these extensions.

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- N/A

#### Bug Fixes

- N/A

### Validation Steps

@:critical

This change is only to dev dependencies. I did these checks locally:

- Root `eslint` on the `src` folders of the 17 extensions gives the same result as `main` (4 errors from before this change, in `positron-r` and `positron-reticulate`).
- `npm ci` passes in clean copies of `open-remote-wsl`, `positron-zed`, and `positron-data-driver-sqlite`.
- `npm ls --package-lock-only` gives the same result as `main` for each extension.

title: Detect Snowflake connections from connections.toml, place connected dot before Detected badge, and hide summaries notice when summary panel is collapsed
description: ### Summary This PR fixes three issues in the Data Connections pane and the Data Explorer. Fixes #16238 Fixes #16239 Fixes #16240 ### Keep the Detected badge and connected dot in fixed columns (#16238) On detected connections in the Data Connections pane, the **DETECTED** badge comes before the green connected dot. Every row keeps space for the dot, even when it isn't connected, so the badge and the dot each stay in the same column down the pane. Before: After: ### Hide the "Summaries unavailable" notice when the summary panel is collapsed (#16239) When column summaries can't be calculated and the table summary panel is collapsed, the notice and its grid row are no longer rendered. Before, the notice's warning icon was still painted, clipped, next to the splitter. Expanding the panel shows the notice again. The notice normally stays in place during a retry so the grid doesn't resize and cancel it, but that doesn't apply here: collapsing already resizes the grid to zero width. ### Detect Snowflake connections from connections.toml (#16240) Every named connection in `connections.toml` now appears in the Data Connections pane as a detected connection, the same way ODBC DSNs from `odbc.ini` already do. - **Detected rows:** each connection gets the **Detected** badge and a stable ID (`snowflake-connection:`), so it keeps its identity and expansion state across restarts. - **Descriptions:** each row is described as `account/database/schema`, using whichever parts the entry has. An entry with no account shows "No account configured". - **No secrets copied:** the detected connection carries only its name. Credentials are read from the file at connect time. - **Live refresh:** the extension watches `connections.toml` (at `$SNOWFLAKE_HOME` if set, otherwise `~/.snowflake`) and re-registers the driver when the file changes, following the same pattern as the ODBC watcher. - **Only re-register on a real change:** re-registering closes open Snowflake connections, so it happens only when the connections defined in the file actually change. - **One snapshot:** the Connections File picker and the detected rows are built from the same read of the file, so they always agree. - **Quiet until used:** nothing is logged on the first registration, so the Snowflake output channel doesn't appear for users who never use Snowflake. ### Release Notes #### Bug Fixes - Snowflake connections defined in `connections.toml` now show up as detected connections in the Data Connections pane. Editing the file updates the list without closing open connections, and a file that fails to parse keeps the last good list (#16238) - The **DETECTED** badge and the green connected dot now stay in the same columns on every row in the Data Connections pane, whether or not the row is connected (#16238) - The Data Explorer no longer shows the summaries notice when the summary panel is collapsed, and collapsing or expanding the panel no longer makes the summary grid jump (#16238) - ### Known limitations - Only `$SNOWFLAKE_HOME/connections.toml` or `~/.snowflake/connections.toml` is read. Other locations the Snowflake CLI supports, such as platform config folders and a `[connections]` section in `config.toml`, are not handled yet. - A credential-only edit to `connections.toml`, such as rotating a token, counts as a change and closes open Snowflake connections. - A briefly invalid or half-written `connections.toml` reads as "no connections" until the next valid save. ### QA Notes - **Connected dot:** connect to a detected connection (an ODBC DSN or a Snowflake connection) and check that the green dot appears before the **Detected** badge, and that the badges line up on connected and disconnected rows. - **Summaries notice:** open a data source in the Data Explorer whose summaries fail to calculate, collapse the summary panel, and check that no warning icon remains beside the splitter. Expand the panel and check that the notice comes back. - **Snowflake detection:** add a few named connections to `~/.snowflake/connections.toml` and check that they appear as detected connections with `account/database/schema` descriptions. Then edit the file while Positron is running (add, remove, and rename a connection) and check that the pane updates without a reload. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Bundle `snowflake-sdk` in the Snowflake data driver and update file-count budgets
description:
Addresses #16025

This PR makes the Snowflake data driver ship 7 files instead of 4,590, and updates the file-count budgets to match.

**Pre-bundle `snowflake-sdk` in its own esbuild entry point.** The driver kept `snowflake-sdk` external, so its entire production dependency closure shipped in the extension's `node_modules`. esbuild now bundles the SDK into a second entry point, `dist/snowflakeSdk.js` (3.5 MB minified), and `positron-data-driver-snowflake` is removed from `extensionsWithNpmDeps`, so no `node_modules` ships. A new `.vscodeignore` keeps `src/`, `out/`, `tsconfig.json`, and the build scripts out of the package.

The SDK stays behind the driver's existing lazy load: `snowflakeClient.ts` imports `./snowflakeSdk.js`, a thin shim that re-exports the SDK, with a dynamic import on the first connection attempt, so activating the extension still does not parse the SDK. `./snowflakeSdk.js` stays external in `extension.js` so that import remains a real deferred load. esbuild runs with `legalComments: 'eof'`, so the license comments in the SDK's dependencies survive minification.

| Extension | Files before | Files after |
|---|---|---|
| `positron-data-driver-snowflake` | 4,590 | 7 |

**Minicore: no native binaries ship.** snowflake-sdk ships nine platform variants of a native minicore binary. The only consumer of the minicore status is Snowflake's in-band telemetry (`CORE_VERSION`, `CORE_FILE_NAME`, `CORE_LOAD_ERROR`, and a `minicore_error` event); no data-path feature uses it. The SDK loads minicore in a try/catch at module load, treats a missing binary as an expected outcome for bundled apps, and honors `SNOWFLAKE_DISABLE_MINICORE`. This PR therefore ships no `.node` files, and the loader degrades gracefully.

**Budget changes** in `build/lib/positron-path-budget.ts`:

- Remove the `positron-data-driver-snowflake` entry (7 files, under the default budget of 100).
- Lower `EXTENSIONS_FILE_COUNT_BUDGET` from 28,000 to 23,000. The expected count is about 20,900.

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- N/A

#### Bug Fixes

- N/A

### Validation Steps

@:connections

The data-connections e2e suite exercises the Snowflake driver against a real backend. Note that it loads the extensions from source with the full `node_modules`, so it cannot find a module that is missing from the packaged build. For that reason, I also did these checks:

- A standalone bundle of `snowflake-sdk` with the extension's esbuild options builds with zero warnings. The only dynamic require in the SDK is the minicore loader's `eval('require')`, and the version read is a static `require` of `package.json` that esbuild inlines.
- The built `dist/extension.js` and `dist/snowflakeSdk.js` work from a directory with no `node_modules` (with `vscode` and `positron` stubbed): the extension module loads, `createConnection` works, and `connectAsync` performs a real network round trip (a nonexistent account fails with error code 401002, as expected).
- `tsc --noEmit` passes for the extension, and the dev path (compiled `out/`, `defaultConnectionFactory`) returns a constructible connection through the new shim.
- The build tests pass: `cd build && node --test lib/test/positron-path-budget.test.ts lib/test/positron-check-path-lengths.test.ts`.

To check by hand in a packaged build:

1. Open the Data Connections pane and connect to a Snowflake account. Browse schemas and tables.
2. Look at the `File counts:` lines in the build log. `positron-data-driver-snowflake` should report 7, and the `extensions/` total should be about 20,900.

title: Block `REditorSupport.r-syntax` to prevent Rmd chunk execution breakage
description:
Fixes #16265

Adds `reditorsupport.r-syntax` (the vscode-R-syntax extension) to the Positron extension blocklist, alongside the other REditorSupport extensions. vscode-R-syntax registers `.Rmd` files under its own `rmd` language ID, which wins the file association over the Quarto extension's `quarto` language and breaks R Markdown chunk execution ("Cannot execute code because there is no registered runtime for the 'rmd' language"). The extension only provides syntax highlighting, which Positron already ships for R and R Markdown, so no functionality is lost. The blocklist vitest suite is extended accordingly. See [the issue](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/16265#issuecomment-5872283815) for a fuller explanation of the language association collision and why fixing it in the third-party extensions is not tenable for us.

### Release Notes

#### New Features
- N/A

#### Bug Fixes
- Blocked the `vscode-R-syntax` extension from being installed, since it breaks R Markdown chunk execution (#16265). Note that the blocklist prevents new installs only. Users who already have `vscode-R-syntax` installed will need to disable or uninstall it manually.

### Validation Steps

@:extensions

1. Open the Extensions view, search for "R Syntax" by REditorSupport, and attempt to install it (or install the VSIX for `reditorsupport.r-syntax`)
2. Verify installation is refused with a message stating the extension conflicts with Positron built-in features
3. Open an `.Rmd` file and verify it opens in the Quarto language mode and chunks run as expected

title: Replace `decompress` with `yauzl` in Ark and Kallichore install scripts
description:
This PR replaces the `decompress` dev dependency with `yauzl` in the install scripts for Ark and Kallichore. It is a follow-up to #16236, and part of setting us up for posit-dev/positron-builds#1269.

### Summary

`decompress` has a critical advisory with no fix. After some other easy-ish fixes, it would be the only critical advisory in `positron-r` and in `positron-supervisor`. Only two scripts use it:

- `extensions/positron-r/scripts/install-kernel.ts`, which installs Ark
- `extensions/positron-supervisor/scripts/install-kallichore-server.ts`, which installs Kallichore

These scripts extract flat zip files that contain one binary and its license files. For this reason, a full archive library is not necessary. The scripts now use `yauzl` 3.4.0, which `positron-duckdb` already uses inside of our project. `yauzl` has no advisories and has one dependency (`pend`). AT LEAST FOR NOW. 😩 

The changes are:

- **Scripts:** A small `extractZip()` helper replaces the call to `decompress()`. The helper keeps the Unix file mode from the archive, so the binaries stay executable. Zip files made on Windows have no Unix mode, so these files get `0644`. `yauzl` rejects entries with absolute paths or `..` segments, which stops a "zip slip" attack.
- **Dependencies:** `decompress` and `@types/decompress` change to `yauzl` and `@types/yauzl` in `devDependencies`.
- **Lockfiles:** The changes remove 31 packages from `positron-r` and 49 packages from `positron-supervisor`. The only version change is `yauzl` from 2.10.0 to 3.4.0. `@vscode/vsce` in `positron-r` keeps its own copy of `yauzl` 2.

The two extensions do not share script code, so each script has its own copy of the helper. If someone feels strongly about not keeping two copies, I am certainly flexible on this.

npm audit results:

| Manifest | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `positron-r` | 1 critical, 2 high | 0 critical, 2 high |
| `positron-supervisor` | 1 critical, 2 high | 0 critical, 2 high |

There are no changes to runtime dependencies or to code that we ship.

### Not in this PR

- `positron-r` still has high advisories for `js-yaml` and `serialize-javascript`, from `mocha@11`.
- `positron-supervisor` still has high advisories for `axios` and `form-data`. These are runtime dependencies, so a separate PR will need to update them.

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- N/A

#### Bug Fixes

- N/A

### Validation Steps

@:critical @:win

This change is only to dev dependencies and build scripts. I did these checks locally on macOS:

- I removed `resources/ark` and `resources/kallichore`. Then I ran `npm run install-kernel` and `npm run install-kallichore`. The extracted files are the same as the output of `unzip`. `ark` and `kcserver` are executable and start correctly.
- I replaced `kcserver` with a file that is not executable, and I ran the install again. The script replaced the file, and the new binary is executable.
- I extracted a Windows zip for Kallichore. The files have the mode `0644`.
- I extracted a zip that has a `../` entry. The helper rejected the zip, and it wrote no files outside the target folder.

CI builds and the Windows tests run these scripts on Linux and Windows.

title: Fix local release builds: don't count source maps
description:
Local release builds fail at the packaging step since #16185 added per-extension file-count budgets.

E.g. I'm seeing this fail:

```
$ npm run gulp vscode-darwin-arm64
...

[15:10:01] 4 file count(s) are over budget:
[15:10:01]   10,270 of 8,500  copilot
[15:10:01]   5,867 of 5,050  positron-data-driver-snowflake
[15:10:01]   3,495 of 3,460  positron-data-driver-databricks
[15:10:01]   574 of 550  positron-data-driver-odbc
```

This appears to be because budgets were set from CI builds. CI builds strip `.js.map` and `.css.map` files during packaging, but local builds keep them, so local builds have many more files in some extensions and go over budget.

This PR leaves source maps out of the budgets, the same way gzip copies from web server builds are already left out. The budgets now fit both local and CI builds, and the numbers themselves don't change.

### Release Notes

#### New Features
- N/A

#### Bug Fixes
- N/A

### Validation Steps

@:critical

1. Run a local release build (for example `npm run gulp vscode-darwin-arm64`) and check that the file-count check passes.
2. `build/lib/test/positron-check-path-lengths.test.ts` now covers source maps along with gzip copies.

description: ## Summary The goal is for the updated skill to require less back and forth with an agent to get a stylized SVG. I reworked the skill that creates the stylized SVGs for us so that there are scripts (1) to help extract icons and align them with text, and (2) to find and fix common positioning problems within the SVGs before generating the final version. I think our SVGs will be more consistent when it comes to image dimensions, colors used, overall sizing of elements within SVG, etc with the changes as well. I tested the updated skill using Claude and Codex with the following findings: - Codex did a great job of creating an SVG in one request without requiring a screenshot of the UI. - Claude did a poor job of creating the SVG in one request without a screenshot of the UI. - Claude did an okay job of creating an SVG in one request with a screenshot of the UI. It would often get the alignment of icons/buttons/text wrong but was easy to correct in another 1-2 requests. ### Changes - Deletes the `positron-abstract-svg` skill and adds `positron-stylized-svg` in its place, which sources icons and colors directly from the checkout (`scripts/extract_icon.py`, `scripts/validate_svg.py`) instead of a hand-maintained reference file. - Adds a QA step for checking title/action-icon overlap in narrow panel headers, the one gap found while comparing output from both skills. ## Skill layout The skill lives in `.agents/skills/` so any agent can read it, not just Claude Code. `.claude/skills/positron-stylized-svg` is a symlink so Claude can find the skill. ## Test plan - [ ] Generated a source-control walkthrough SVG with each skill from the same prompt and compared them side by side. **Codex - no screenshot** **Claude - no screenshot** **Claude - provided screenshot + 2 additional requests**

title: Bump dependencies in `open-remote-ssh` lockfile for security
description: This PR updates `package-lock.json` in `open-remote-ssh` to remove all npm audit advisories in this extension. The change is only in the lockfile, with no changes to `package.json`. All new versions are inside the semver ranges that we already declare. This is a follow-up to #16203, which did not include the `ip-address` update for this extension. ### Summary I ran `npm audit fix --package-lock-only`. The runtime changes are: - `socks` 2.8.3 to 2.8.10. With this patch bump, `socks` uses `ip-address` 10.7.2 instead of 9.0.5. This removes two high advisories: XSS in `Address6`, and SSRF from leading-zero octets in `Address4`. - `minimatch` 10.2.2 to 10.2.6 and `brace-expansion` 5.0.2 to 5.0.12, both from `glob`. These remove the high ReDoS and DoS advisories. - `@babel/runtime-corejs3` 7.25.0 to 7.29.7, from `simple-socks`. This removes one moderate advisory. The other changes are dev dependencies (`ajv`, `brace-expansion@1`, `flatted`, and more). Some of these are the same as the changes for this extension in #16203. The two PRs merge with no conflicts. The extension uses `socks` in one place, `src/authResolver.ts`, to connect through the local SOCKS tunnel. The proxy and the destination are both `127.0.0.1`. Thus the `ip-address` advisories are not reachable in practice. Dynamic forwarding is on by default, so each remote SSH connection uses this code. | Scope | Moderate | High | Critical | |---|---|---|---| | All dependencies, before | 4 | 6 | 0 | | All dependencies, after | 0 | 0 | 0 | | Runtime only, before | 2 | 3 | 0 | | Runtime only, after | 0 | 0 | 0 | `npm ci` and `tsc -p ./` pass for the extension. I also connected to a remote host with a dev build that has these changes: ### Release Notes #### New Features - N/A #### Bug Fixes - Update dependencies of the Remote SSH extension to remove known security vulnerabilities ### Validation Steps @:remote-ssh Connect to a remote host with _Remote-SSH: Connect to Host..._. title: Notification on connection to Databricks with REH
description: Fixes posit-dev/positron-builds#1192 ### Summary Adds detection of the Databricks compute environment when connecting over SSH. Before installing the server on a remote host, `open-remote-ssh` probes the host for a small set of environment variables (`DATABRICKS_RUNTIME_VERSION`, `DATABRICKS_CLUSTER_ID`, `DATABRICKS_REMOTE_ENV`), reading only variable names, never values. `DATABRICKS_HOST` and `DATABRICKS_TOKEN` are excluded from detection. A host that also carries a Posit Workbench marker (`RS_SERVER_URL`) is never flagged. When Databricks is detected, a warning toast is shown, and the verdict is appended as an `ssh-env` query parameter on the REH download URL when the URL points at `cdn.posit.co`. Also updates `getVSCodeServerConfig` to fall back to the latest published dailies version when running unbuilt, since a dev instance's build number is `0`. ### Release Notes #### New Features - N/A #### Bug Fixes - Warn when connecting over SSH to a Databricks compute environment, which the Positron license does not permit (posit-dev/positron-builds#1192) ### Validation Steps @:remote-ssh The new detection and URL-construction logic is unit tested in `extensions/open-remote-ssh/src/common/sshEnvironment.vitest.ts` (`npx vitest run extensions/open-remote-ssh/src/common/sshEnvironment.vitest.ts`), covering the Databricks signals, the Workbench exclusion, client-credential-only hosts, and the CDN URL matching/param-appending rules. For a manual check against a real cluster (see [setting up Databricks compute](https://connect.posit.it/positron-wiki/dev-notes/remote-ssh-databricks.html) for setup steps): 1. Connect to a Databricks cluster over Remote-SSH. 2. Verify a warning toast appears: "Connected to a Databricks environment. The Positron license prohibits embedding, installing, or executing Positron within a managed SaaS compute environment provided by a third party. ..." 3. Verify the connection still succeeds. 4. Connect to an ordinary (non-Databricks) host and confirm no toast appears. 5. If you have access to CDN logs, confirm the download request carries `?ssh-env=databricks` for the Databricks case and no such parameter otherwise.

title: Remove unused `mocha` from Positron extensions and bump `positron-r` to `mocha` 11
description:
This PR removes the unused `mocha@9` dev dependency from 18 Positron extensions, and bumps `positron-r` to `mocha@11`. It is a follow-up to #16189 and #16203, and part of setting us up for posit-dev/positron-builds#1269.

### Summary

Nineteen Positron extensions currently declare `"mocha": "^9.2.1"`. This one dev dependency brings in advisories for `nanoid`, `serialize-javascript`, `js-yaml`, `minimatch`, and `diff`. These advisories were most of the high advisories that were left after #16203. This version of `mocha` does not come from upstream: `copilot` is the only upstream extension that declares `mocha`, and it uses `^11.7.1`.

These extensions do not use their own copy of `mocha`. `npm run test-extension` runs `vscode-test` from the repository root, which uses the root `mocha`. The types come from `@types/mocha`, which does not change in this PR.

- **18 extensions:** I removed `mocha` from `devDependencies`. The lockfile changes are removals only.
- **`positron-r`:** `src/test/index.ts` imports `mocha` to run tests from `launch.json` in a debug session. For this reason, I bumped `mocha` from `^9.2.1` to `^11.8.0` and did not remove it. `extensions/positron-python` already uses `mocha@11`.

There are no changes here to runtime dependencies or to code that we ship.

npm audit results for 41 Positron-owned manifests:

| Scope | Critical | High | Moderate | Low |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| All dependencies, before | 3 | 129 | 21 | 27 |
| All dependencies, after | 3 | 43 | 22 | 10 |

The number of manifests with a high or critical advisory decreases from 24 to 15. The runtime results do not change.

### Not in this PR

- `js-yaml`: 8 extensions have a high advisory from `eslint@8`. The fix is in our current semver ranges, so a lockfile-only follow-up can remove it.
- `positron-r`: `mocha@11` still has one high advisory (`serialize-javascript`). The fix is `mocha@12`, which is ESM only and requires Node 20.19 or later. The debug runner in `positron-r` is CommonJS, so this change needs more work.

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- N/A

#### Bug Fixes

- N/A

### Validation Steps

@:critical

This change is only to dev dependencies. I did these checks locally:

- `npm run build-check` reports 0 errors.
- Extension host tests pass for `positron-r` (207), `next-edit-suggestions` (59), `positron-duckdb` (59), `positron-supervisor` (53), `positron-zed` (2), and the Databricks, DuckDB, pins, PostgreSQL, Redshift, ODBC, Snowflake, and SQLite drivers.
- In `positron-run-app`, the same test also fails on `main`.

To make sure that the `positron-r` debug runner works with `mocha@11`, start the "positron-r extension tests" launch configuration from the Run and Debug view.

title: Bump dependencies in extension lockfiles for security
description:
This PR updates `package-lock.json` in 25 Positron-owned manifests to remove npm audit advisories. This set of changes is only in the lockfiles, with no changes to `package.json`; all new versions are inside the semver ranges that we already declare. This is a follow-up to #16189, and part of us being able to set up posit-dev/positron-builds#1269 for success.

### Summary

The PR has two commits:

1. **Dev dependencies (22 extensions).** I ran `npm audit fix --package-lock-only`. In 8 manifests, that command also changed runtime packages. For those manifests, I used `npm update` on only the vulnerable dev packages. All changed entries in this commit are dev dependencies.
2. **Runtime dependencies (5 manifests).** I did a conservative set of runtime bumps in `next-edit-suggestions`, `positron-pdf-server`, `positron-proxy`, `positron-r`, and the `pr-test-checker` action. All runtime changes are patch or minor bumps of small libraries: `body-parser`, `qs`, `raw-body`, `follow-redirects`, `semver`, `brace-expansion`, and `minimatch`.

npm audit results for 41 Positron-owned manifests (`positron-dev-containers` is in #16189):

| Scope | Critical | High | Moderate | Low |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| All dependencies, before | 11 | 283 | 113 | 61 |
| All dependencies, after | 3 | 137 | 32 | 29 |
| Runtime only, before | 0 | 29 | 24 | 4 |
| Runtime only, after | 0 | 23 | 20 | 1 |

### Not in this PR

These runtime changes are larger, so they will go in separate PRs:

- `positron-supervisor`: `axios` 1.16 to 1.20 adds `https-proxy-agent`, which changes proxy behavior for kernel connections.
- `positron-catalog-explorer`: `@azure/msal-node` 3 to 6 and `@azure/msal-browser` 4 to 5.
- `positron-ipywidgets/renderer`: a large JupyterLab and Lumino update, with `htmlparser2` 8 to 12 and `@jupyter/ydoc` 3 to 4.
- `open-remote-ssh`: `ip-address` 9 to 10.
- `authentication`: changes to AWS SDK internals.
- The `e2e-failure-analyzer` action: `@anthropic-ai/sdk` 0.81 to 0.93.

Most of the remaining dev advisories come from `mocha@9`, which pins its own versions of `js-yaml`, `nanoid`, `minimatch`, and `serialize-javascript`. The fix for these is a major version bump of `mocha` in `package.json`. Some advisories (`snowflake-sdk`, `toml`, `decompress`, `@jupyterlab/*`) have no fix without a major version change.

### Release Notes

- Update dependencies of Positron extensions to remove known security vulnerabilities

Positron should... still work.

title: Bundle express in the proxy and PDF server extensions and update file-count budgets
description:
Addresses #16025

This PR makes two extensions ship fewer files, and it fixes a file-count budget test that fails on `main`.

**Bundle `express` in `positron-proxy` and `positron-pdf-server`.** Both extensions kept `express` external, so each one shipped the full `express` dependency tree in its own `node_modules`. This was a carry-over from the old webpack configs, and no reason for it was recorded. esbuild now bundles `express` with no warnings. The two extensions are removed from `extensionsWithNpmDeps`, so they no longer ship `node_modules`. Each extension also gets a `.vscodeignore` in the style of the upstream esbuild extensions, so `src/`, `out/`, `tsconfig.json`, and the build scripts do not ship.

| Extension | Files before | Files after |
|---|---|---|
| `positron-proxy` | 755 | 7 |
| `positron-pdf-server` | 956 | 408 |

The "after" counts come from `vsce.listFiles` with the new configuration. Of the 408 files in `positron-pdf-server`, 402 are the pdf.js viewer assets in `pdfjs-dist/`. A later PR can prune them.

**Fix the budget test on `main`.** #16214 removed the catalog explorer extension, and #16185 merged after it with a budget entry for `positron-catalog-explorer`. The test "each entry names a directory that ships" now fails on `main`. The release-build check does not fail, because it reads budgets only for extensions that ship. This PR removes the entry.

**Budget changes** in `build/lib/positron-path-budget.ts`:

- Remove `positron-catalog-explorer` (extension removed) and `positron-proxy` (now below the default budget of 100).
- Lower `positron-pdf-server` from 1,050 to 450.
- Lower the `extensions/` total from 34,000 to 28,000. The expected count is about 25,500.

The bundled `express` keeps its license banners, because esbuild keeps `/*!` comments by default. `http-proxy-middleware` is already bundled into `positron-proxy` in the same way.

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- N/A

#### Bug Fixes

- N/A

### Validation Steps

@:pdf @:viewer @:help @:apps @:web

These E2E suites use the proxy and the PDF server. Note that they load the extensions from source with the full `node_modules`, so they cannot find a module that is missing from the packaged build. For that reason, I also did these checks:

- The build tests pass: `cd build && node --test lib/test/positron-path-budget.test.ts lib/test/positron-check-path-lengths.test.ts`.
- Neither built `dist/extension.js` contains `require("express")`.
- I bundled `express` and `http-proxy-middleware` with the same esbuild options and ran the bundle from a directory with no `node_modules`. Static files had the correct content types, `sendFile` worked, a missing file returned 404, and a proxied request worked.

To test by hand in a packaged build:

1. Open a PDF file. Make sure that the viewer shows the PDF and its toolbar.
2. Run a Shiny or Streamlit app. Make sure that it shows in the Viewer.
3. Open a help topic in the Help pane. Make sure that it shows correctly.
4. Look at the `File counts:` lines in the build log. Make sure that the `positron-proxy` and `positron-pdf-server` counts match the table above.

title: fix(supervisor): prune stale tombstones on TID collision and shutdown socket errors
description:
Fixes #16167.

## Root cause (verified in a Linux Docker deployment)

Two defects combine into permanent tombstones:

1. `isProcessAlive` uses `kill(pid, 0)`. On Linux, thread IDs share the PID number space, so it succeeds for a worker thread (e.g. `tokio-rt-worker`) that recycled a dead supervisor's PID — auto-prune is skipped.
2. `handleShutdownAction` calls `removeByPid` only on the success path. When the socket is already gone (`ENOENT`), execution jumps to `catch`, the entry is never removed, and Shut Down always fails the same way.

Worst case: a supervisor killed with `kill -9`/OOM never unlinks its socket, so **both** `existsSync` and `kill(pid, 0)` return true simultaneously.

## Changes (`extensions/positron-supervisor`)

- `showRunningSupervisors` now prunes via new `isSupervisorAlive(pid, socketPath)`: `kill(pid, 0)` + socket must exist + on Linux only, `/proc/<pid>/comm` must be `kcserver` (zero-dependency, `pidfd_open` would need native bindings).
- `handleShutdownAction` drops the registry entry when shutdown fails with `ENOENT`/`ECONNREFUSED` (conservative: timeouts on live supervisors still keep the entry).
- New `src/test/supervisorLiveness.test.ts` (4 cases) for the existing harness.

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit` clean on the extension; eslint not runnable in this sandbox (no local binary, registry blocked) — CI lint will cover it.
- `/proc` comm behavior verified empirically in a CentOS 7 container: worker thread reads as `tokio-rt-worker`, live supervisor as `kcserver`.

title: List providers with descriptions vertically in a fixed-height dialog
description:
Reworks the provider picker in the **Add Data Connection** dialog from a fixed-height card grid into a list of rows, each carrying the driver's name, its one-line description, and its own **Connect** button. The description is the part that matters for the issue: previously the grid showed a logo and a name, so "ODBC" or "Posit Connect Pins" had to explain itself from four words of label. The row layout mirrors the Configure LLM Providers modal, so the two provider-picking surfaces in the product now read as one.

Fixes #15126

### Notes for reviewers

**The dialog is a fixed height, deliberately.** `LIST_CONTENT_HEIGHT` is passed as both `contentMinHeight` and `contentMaxHeight`, so the box is one size regardless of how many drivers are registered. This is not just an aesthetic choice: drivers arrive asynchronously (each is registered by its own extension's `activate()`), while `PositronDynamicModalDialog` centers itself once, in a layout effect on mount. A content-sized box would therefore be centered against an empty list and then grow downward, off the bottom of a shorter window. Fixing the height removes the race rather than papering over it.

The height is 324px, which is six rows: `6×36 + 5×20 + 4 + 20 − 16`. Every term is a whole row, so the arithmetic only holds while a row is exactly 36px tall — both the icon plate and the name/description stack are pinned to that height in the CSS, and the constant's comment says so. Eight drivers ship by default, so the stock list scrolls by two; the fold lands cleanly between rows rather than on a sliver of the next one.

**The row classes are named `provider-row*`, not `driver-list-item*`.** The older Connections pane declares `.driver-list-item` *unscoped* in `positronConnections/.../listDriversState.css`, which is live in the workbench stylesheet. Scoping under `.select-data-connection-provider` wins on specificity for every property redeclared, but anything that rule sets and this one does not still leaks through — its `cursor: pointer` above all, which would have put a hand cursor on a row whose only interactive element is the button. A distinct name ends the whole class of leak instead of the one property that happened to be visible.

**The e2e provider selector keys off the Connect button's accessible name.** Rows now render descriptions, and the ODBC extension describes its per-database drivers as "Connect to a {name} database over ODBC" — so filtering rows by the substring `ODBC` matches every one of them on a machine with ODBC drivers installed, and `toBeVisible()` throws a strict-mode violation. `DataConnections.providerConnectButton()` matches `Connect to {name}` exactly instead, and is shared by `selectProvider()` and the new `expectProviderVisible()`. Driver names are unique across extensions: `odbcDatabases.ts` marks the five profiles that would collide with a standalone driver (PostgreSQL, Redshift, Snowflake, Databricks, SQLite) `registerDriver: false` for exactly this reason.

Also in here: the "provider is no longer available" message is cleared when the driver list changes, so it can't go stale after a registration, and it carries `role='alert'` — a failed Connect leaves the dialog where it is and focus on the button, so nothing else would announce it.

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- N/A

#### Bug Fixes

- N/A

### Validation Steps

@:connections @:workbench

1. Open the **Data Connections** pane and click **Add Connection**.
2. Confirm each provider row shows a logo, a name, and a description, and that the rows are evenly spaced with the list ending on a whole row rather than a partial one.
3. Confirm the dialog is the same size whether it is opened immediately on a cold window (drivers still registering) or after they have all loaded — it should not resize or jump as the list fills in.
4. Resize the window shorter and reopen the dialog; confirm it stays on screen and centered.
5. Confirm the row itself is not clickable and shows no hand cursor — only the **Connect** button is interactive, and it advances to the configure step for the right provider.
6. Confirm the title bar's close button dismisses the dialog (there is no longer a Next/Cancel footer).
7. Click **Back** from the mechanism step (e.g. via PostgreSQL) and confirm the provider list returns at the same size and position.

Worth a look on a machine with ODBC drivers configured, since that is what pushes the list past the fold and exercises scrolling.

title: Add per-extension file-count budgets to packaging checks
description:
A first step toward addressing #16025!

This PR adds a file-count check to the packaged build. It does not remove any files. It records the current counts as a baseline and sets a budget for each extension, so that each later PR shows its reduction as a smaller number in a budget that is already in the code.

### Summary

An installed Positron has about 34,000 files. About 30,000 of them are in `extensions/`. A high file count makes startup scans, installs, upgrades, backups, and antivirus scans slow on network filesystems. Posit Workbench runs the server (REH) build on such filesystems, so this PR checks the server build as well as the desktop build.

- `build/lib/positron-check-path-lengths.ts` now walks the packaged tree one time and does two checks. The first is the Windows MAX_PATH check from #14702, which does not change. The second is a new file-count check.
- The file-count check logs the files and bytes for all of `extensions/`, for each extension, and for the shared `extensions/node_modules`. It also logs the 20 largest `node_modules` packages of each large extension. A nested dependency counts toward the top-level package that pulls it in.
- `build/lib/positron-path-budget.ts` holds the budgets:
  - One budget for each of the 19 directories that ship more than 100 files. Each budget is the 2026.10.0-85 darwin-arm64 count plus about 10%. A comment on each entry gives the count.
  - A default budget of 100 files for each extension that has no entry. A new large extension then fails the build until it gets a reviewed entry.
  - A budget of 33,400 files for `extensions/` as a whole.
- The desktop build already ran the path-length check. The server build (`gulpfile.reh.ts`) now runs both checks too.
- If the build cannot find the `extensions/` directory, the check fails. It does not pass on an empty tree.

### Baseline (2026.10.0-85, darwin-arm64)

| Extension | Files | Budget |
|---|---|---|
| copilot | 7,728 | 8,500 |
| positron-python | 5,219 | 5,750 |
| positron-data-driver-snowflake | 4,590 | 5,050 |
| positron-catalog-explorer | 4,140 | 4,560 |
| positron-data-driver-databricks | 3,145 | 3,460 |
| positron-pdf-server | 956 | 1,050 |
| positron-proxy | 755 | 830 |
| All of `extensions/` | 30,297 | 33,400 |

### How to find the counts in a build log

The packaging step of each build prints the counts. Search the log for `File counts:`. The output has this shape:

```
File counts: 30,297 files (1082.8 MB) in extensions/, budget 33,400; 34,331 files (2745.2 MB) shipped in total
    7,728 of  8,500   220.6 MB  copilot
          804     1.4 MB  @sinclair/typebox
          505     1.6 MB  @anthropic-ai/sdk
    ...
    1,066 files in 110 other extension(s), each within 100
```

Each extension line gives the file count, the "budget", the size in bytes, and the name. The indented lines below it are its largest packages. The `Path lengths ok:` line just before it is the MAX_PATH result.

If a count is over budget, the build fails. The log then shows a list that starts with `file count(s) are over budget:`, and it names each extension that is over budget.

You can see this locally by running `npm run gulp vscode-darwin-arm64` (or a different platform). The counts are near the end of the output.

I will kick off a few of our build action to see it in action there.

### How the later PRs use this

Each later PR to address #16025 will make one extension smaller. In each PR:

1. Build the package for at least one platform (prioritizing Linux, because of Workbench).
2. Find the extension's line after `File counts:` and record the new count.
3. Change the extension's budget in `positron-path-budget.ts` to the new count plus about 10%. Then change the total budget for `extensions/` by the same amount.
4. Put the before and after counts in the PR description.

The package lines show where the files come from. For example, the copilot lines show `@azure/*`, `@sinclair/typebox`, and `@anthropic-ai/sdk`. These packages are already inside `dist/extension.js`, so their copies in `node_modules` do not have to ship.

### Before merge

The budgets come from one platform. Windows and Linux can ship more native binaries, for example the ODBC driver and the Snowflake `.node` files. Before this PR merges, I will read the counts from the Linux builds that the tags above start. If a budget is too small for a platform, I will raise it.

### QA Notes

This PR changes only the build. It does not change the product.

- `cd build && node --test 'lib/test/positron-*.test.ts'` passes (17 tests). The new tests use a small tree on disk to confirm the counts for each extension and package, the three types of budget failure, and the error when the `extensions/` directory is wrong. A test also confirms that each budget entry names an extension that exists in the repo.
- The check ran against the installed 2026.10.0-85 macOS app. It finished in about 0.5 seconds and passed.

title: ci: remove the soft-fail e2e tag and its CI plumbing
description:
Removes the soft-fail e2e tag and all of the CI plumbing that supported it.

### Summary

The soft-fail tag was only honored by the merge-to-main workflow (`test-merge.yml` passed `allow_soft_fail: true` to the electron, chromium, and Windows lanes). Every PR, full-suite, and nightly lane already ran with it disabled, and positron-builds never called the check script at all.

Data from the last 30 days of merge-to-main runs (100 runs, 700 shard logs):

| Measure | Count |
|---|---|
| Hard failures after retries, untagged | 105 |
| Hard failures after retries, soft-fail tagged | 0 |
| Runs where the tag turned a red job green | 0 |
| Flakes that passed on retry, soft-fail tagged | 9 of 242 |

The tag never changed a job's outcome, so this PR removes it:

- Drops the `SpecialTags` enum (soft-fail was its only member) and the tag from 13 test files. Several of those suites were already fully skipped.
- Removes the `allow_soft_fail` input from 11 reusable e2e workflows and the values passed by `test-pull-request.yml`, `test-full-suite.yml`, `test-cross-browser.yml`, and `test-merge.yml`.
- Single-job lanes (ubuntu, debian, rocky, sles, suse) now run Playwright directly and let its exit code decide.
- Renames `scripts/check-soft-fail-failures.js` to `scripts/check-e2e-failures.js` with the soft-fail branch removed. The report jobs in the sharded lanes still need it because shard steps end in `|| true` and the merged JSON report decides pass/fail.
- Removes the Soft-Failed Tests section from the Slack skipped-tests report and updates the tag-lib shell tests, the PR helper tag script, and the e2e triage skill docs.

Merge-to-main behavior change: a failure after retries in one of the formerly tagged tests will now fail the merge job, the same as any other test. Given the numbers above, that is expected to be rare.

title: Set PKG_SYSREQS=false in the Rocky CI images
description:
Addresses the Rocky-only failures of `packages-pane-vulnerabilities.test.ts` ("R - Flags an installed package with an unscored CRAN advisory"), e.g. in [nightly run 35983751579](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron-builds/actions/runs/35983751579). ### Intent On the Rocky web lane, `pak::pkg_install("widgetframe")` runs a dnf system-requirements install (`libuv-devel` for `fs`) before it builds the package. Syncing Rocky's repo metadata alone can outlast the test's install budget, so the list assertion times out while the status bar still says "Installing Packages...". The test passes on every other lane. Over the last 14 days it had a failing attempt in 3 of 10 Rocky runs and 0 of 92 runs elsewhere. ### Approach Set `ENV PKG_SYSREQS=false` in the `rocky_8` and `rocky_9` Dockerfiles, matching what the SLES and openSUSE images already do to carry `pkg.sysreqs=FALSE` into the R sessions the e2e tests drive. Both Rocky images only passed it to their build-time installs. The images are being rebuilt in place at the existing `24.18.0` tag via `ci-images-build-os.yml` on this branch, so no workflow pins change. ### QA Notes No product change. After the images are republished, the Rocky web lane's R security-advisory test should stop timing out on the install step. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ### E2E Triage Diagnosis
🟢 High confidence -- On the Rocky 8 web lane, pak::pkg_install(widgetframe) runs a dnf system-requirements install (libuv-devel for fs) and builds from source; the 30s toast + 60s list wait in the test budget expires while pak is still downloading dnf repo metadata. - **Test:** [Packages Pane - Security Advisories > R - Flags an installed package with an unscored CRAN advisory](https://connect.posit.it/e2e-test-insights/?tab=test_health&repo=positron&test=Packages%20Pane%20-%20Security%20Advisories%20%3E%20R%20-%20Flags%20an%20installed%20package%20with%20an%20unscored%20CRAN%20advisory%7C%7C%7Ctest%2Fe2e%2Ftests%2Fpackages-pane%2Fpackages-pane-vulnerabilities.test.ts) - **Targeted failure:** Pattern A: expectPackageInList(widgetframe) toBeVisible timeout, rhel/chromium only, 3 of 10 runs with a failing attempt. - **Signal:** Error-context snapshot at failure: status bar Installing Packages..., Refresh disabled, progressbar shown, list rendered unfiltered without widgetframe; R console mid dnf install -y dnf-plugins-core with Rocky Linux 8 AppStream 34 MB metadata download. Same in retry. Debian/Ubuntu/SLES/openSUSE 100% pass; SLES/openSUSE images set ENV PKG_SYSREQS=false, rocky_8/rocky_9 do not. - **Frequency:** 5/10 runs (50%) on main, rhel/chromium - **Hypothesis:** Environment/test-budget issue, not a product bug: pak sysreqs is on at runtime in the Rocky images because PKG_SYSREQS is unset, so the install includes a dnf metadata sync + system package install that alone can exceed the 90s budget.

title: Add setting for whether we monitor child processes
description:
Adds a `kernelSupervisor.resourceUsageIncludeChildren` setting that controls whether the CPU and memory numbers reported for a session include the session's child processes. It defaults to `true`, which matches today's behavior.

The supervisor samples resource usage for every session on a timer. Walking a session's process tree is the expensive part of that sampling, so on a machine with an unusual or very large process tree it can be expensive. With the setting off, the supervisor measures only the kernel process itself and skips child enumeration entirely.

The value is passed to the server when it starts and can also be changed while a server is running, in which case the new value is pushed to the running server along with the poll interval. The startup flag is only passed when the setting is off, so a server build that predates the flag still starts normally.

The server side of this lives in posit-dev/kallichore#77. **This PR should not merge until that PR has landed and been released** -- I will update the Kallichore pin here at that point.

The Kallichore change improves the efficiency of child process metric collection to the point that I don't _think_ we will need this flag, but given that we've been wrong before about how expensive metrics collection can be in the wild, it's cheap insurance. 

Fixes #15706.

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- N/A

#### Bug Fixes

- Reduced the supervisor's idle CPU usage, and added a setting to leave child processes out of a session's reported resource usage (#15706)

### Validation Steps

@:sessions

1. Start a Python and an R session and confirm the CPU and memory readout still appears on each console tab.
2. Open settings and turn off **Kernel Supervisor: Resource Usage Include Children**. Confirm the readout keeps updating and does not go blank or stall.
3. From a Python session, start a long-running child process:

```python
import subprocess
p = subprocess.Popen(["python", "-c", "while True: pass"])
```

With the setting on, the session's CPU should climb to reflect the child. With it off, it should not.

4. Turn the setting back on while the session is still running and confirm the child's usage is picked back up without restarting the session or reloading the window.
5. Restart Positron with the setting off and confirm sessions start normally and still report their own usage.

title: e2e: assert on the first matching line in the package helper
description:
Follow-up to #16179, which broke "R - Renv already installed" on the chromium lane in merge run 35883611958. ### Summary #16179 widened the install expectation in `PackageManager.manage` to also accept `trying URL`, so the single-library Windows lane passes. On multi-library platforms R prints both the `Installing package into ...` header and the `trying URL ...` line, each in its own console span. The locator now resolves to two elements and Playwright's strict mode fails the assertion: ``` strict mode violation: getByText(/Installing|Downloading|Fetched|trying URL/) resolved to 2 elements: 1) Installing package into '/usr/local/lib/R/site-li... 2) ... aka getByText('trying URL \'https://') ``` The PR's own Linux electron run passed only because the assertion happened to poll between the two lines. This is not a timeout problem: the console had the output, and the assertion failed on element count, so a longer wait would not change the outcome. The fix asserts on `.first()`, so any number of matching lines proves the install started. The helper still waits for the call to return and confirms `requireNamespace()` afterwards. The comment from #16179 is also trimmed to one line. ### Release Notes #### New Features - N/A #### Bug Fixes - N/A (test infrastructure only) ### Validation Steps @:win @:new-folder-flow @:web "R - Renv already installed" must pass on the Windows lane (single library, only `trying URL` matches) and on the chromium and electron Linux lanes (two matching lines). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ### E2E Triage Diagnosis
🟢 High confidence -- Follow-up: #16179 regex matches two console spans on multi-library R (Installing package into + trying URL), strict mode violation on chromium; assert on .first() - **Test:** [New Folder Flow: R Project > R - Renv already installed](https://connect.posit.it/e2e-test-insights/?tab=test_health&repo=positron&test=New%20Folder%20Flow%3A%20R%20Project%20%3E%20R%20-%20Renv%20already%20installed%7C%7C%7Ctest%2Fe2e%2Ftests%2Fnew-folder-flow%2Fnew-folder-flow-r.test.ts) - **Targeted failure:** strict mode violation: getByText(/Installing|Downloading|Fetched|trying URL/) resolved to 2 elements, ubuntu/chromium, merge run 35883611958 - **Signal:** Failure text lists both spans; PR electron run passed by polling between the two lines; not a timeout - **Frequency:** 4/62 runs (6.5%) on main, win/electron - **Hypothesis:** infra

title: e2e: wait for the kernel to start the sleep in variables-progress
description:
Fixes a race in the Variables progress bar e2e test (`variables-progress.test.ts`), seen on the ubuntu/electron nightly lane. The test pastes `Sys.sleep(20)` into the console and immediately clicks Delete All Variables, expecting the progress bar to show while the clear request waits behind the sleep. `pasteCodeToConsole` returns as soon as Enter is pressed, before the execute request reaches the kernel. In the failing CI run the clear request arrived at the kernel 74 ms before the sleep did, so an idle kernel answered it in under a millisecond and the bar (which only renders after an RPC has been pending for 500 ms) never appeared. The fix makes the long computation print a marker first (`cat("started", "sleeping\n"); Sys.sleep(20)`) and waits for that output before clicking Delete. The marker comes from the kernel, so once it is visible the sleep is running and the clear request queues behind it. Waiting for the console's Interrupt button was tried first and does not work: the button also shows while the code is being submitted, before the kernel reports busy, and the race reproduced locally with that gate in place. No timeouts were changed. ### QA Notes Test-only change. On a Mac the original race reproduced in 3 of 4 local runs; with this change 4 of 4 passed and the kernel log shows the execute request arriving before the clear in every pass. Kernel log evidence from CI and the full triage are in the diagnosis block below. ### Validation Steps @:variables Run `test/e2e/tests/variables/variables-progress.test.ts` on the electron project; both passes should show and then clear the progress bar. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ### E2E Triage Diagnosis
🟢 High confidence -- Test race: the Delete All Variables click reaches the kernel before the pasted Sys.sleep(20) execute_request does, so the clear RPC is answered by an idle kernel in <1 ms and the client-side progress bar (shown only while an RPC is pending >500 ms) never renders. - **Test:** [Variables - Progress bar > Run a long computation and see the progress bar appearing](https://connect.posit.it/e2e-test-insights/?tab=test_health&repo=positron&test=Variables%20-%20Progress%20bar%20%3E%20Run%20a%20long%20computation%20and%20see%20the%20progress%20bar%20appearing%7C%7C%7Ctest%2Fe2e%2Ftests%2Fvariables%2Fvariables-progress.test.ts) - **Targeted failure:** Error: expect(received).toBe(expected) // Object.is equality -- Expected: true, Received: false -- Timeout 5000ms exceeded while waiting on the predicate (variables-progress.test.ts:66, hasProgressBar() toBe(true)) - **Signal:** Kernel log for session 2 (r-fa94cab0): comm_msg 'clear' received 15:19:53.003 and ClearReply sent 15:19:53.004 (busy/idle window ~30us), then execute_request 'Sys.sleep(20)' received 15:19:53.077 -- 74 ms AFTER the clear. Session 1 in the same run shows the intended ordering: Sys.sleep sent to R 15:19:30.259, clear header dated 15:19:30.372 but not picked up by the shell thread until 15:19:50.259 (blocked ~20 s), during which the bar rendered. Trace: pasteCodeToConsole returns 6 ms before the 'Delete all objects' click; no busy check between them. The bar is driven purely by client-side pending-RPC count on the active Variables instance (mainThreadLanguageRuntime setClientStatus(Busy) on send, Idle when pending map empties; variablesCore.tsx debounces 500 ms), so a sub-500 ms clear never creates the element. - **Frequency:** 2/70 runs (2.9%) on main, ubuntu/electron - **Hypothesis:** race
