title: Add MotherDuck as a data connection provider
description: Fixes #15100 ### Summary This PR adds MotherDuck as a provider in the New Connection dialog. Positron reads your MotherDuck access token from the `motherduck_token` environment variable, and the Connections pane shows your MotherDuck databases. You can preview tables, views, and columns from any database in the Data Explorer: The connection dialog generates code for Python (duckdb and SQLAlchemy), R (DBI), and ggsql. The generated code does not contain the token, because the MotherDuck extension reads the same `motherduck_token` variable in your R, Python, or ggsql session. MotherDuck uses the same `@duckdb/node-api` entry point as DuckDB, so I decided to put the MotherDuck driver in the `positron-data-driver-duckdb` extension and have it use the shared `positron-data-explorer-duckdb` backend. The main changes are: - The environment variable is the only way to authenticate in this PR, so the dialog has no token field and stores no secret. If the variable is missing, Connect tells you how to set it. I'll add a pasted token in a followup. - DuckDB workers do not inherit `motherduck_token` from your shell. Only a MotherDuck worker gets the token, from its connection. - The access token goes to the DuckDB worker in an environment variable, not in argv, so other local users cannot see it with `ps`. The worker does not open an `md:` path without a token, because MotherDuck then starts a browser sign-in and blocks. - Each MotherDuck connection has its own worker. The shared worker pool refuses a configuration that has a token, so two accounts never share a worker. - The tree and the Data Explorer previews can use a named database, with three-part names (`"db"."schema"."table"`). The DuckDB file provider still uses the current database. - Errors do not show the token. Connection errors give clear messages for a rejected token, a missing database, a failed extension download, and a timeout. The timeout is 5 minutes, because the first connection also downloads the MotherDuck extension. - MotherDuck has its own Data Explorer handler and its own output channel. - R is not available on Windows. MotherDuck publishes no extension for the R duckdb build on Windows (`windows_amd64_mingw`). The generated ggsql code works with ggsql 0.4.1, but that version opens MotherDuck read-write even when Read Only is selected. I'll do a PR to ggsql to send the read-only mode from the `@connect` URI to DuckDB. I'll handle #16828 in a followup. Also, we can add [further auth methods for MotherDuck](https://motherduck.com/docs/key-tasks/authenticating-and-connecting-to-motherduck/authenticating-to-motherduck/#authentication-using-an-access-token) later. ### Release Notes #### New Features - Add MotherDuck as a data connection provider. Connect with the `motherduck_token` environment variable, browse your databases, preview tables in the Data Explorer, and generate connection code for Python, R, and ggsql (#15100) #### Bug Fixes - N/A ### Validation Steps @:connections @:data-explorer @:duck-db @:win @:web These e2e tests make sure that the DuckDB file provider and pins work as before. MotherDuck needs an account, so CI has no MotherDuck e2e tests. Unit and extension tests cover code generation, token handling, the tree, and previews against local DuckDB. To test MotherDuck manually, you will need to sign up for a MotherDuck account, get an access token in the MotherDuck web UI, put it in an environment variable, etc. I am comfortable with the reviewer not doing that FWIW. If you do, take these steps: 1. Add `export motherduck_token=''` to your shell profile, and restart Positron. (If you happen to have a `~/.motherduck_token` file, move it away first, because the MotherDuck extension also reads that file.) 2. Open the Connections pane, select New Connection, and choose MotherDuck. Connect. 3. Make sure that the pane shows Databases, with `my_db` and `sample_data`. 4. Expand `sample_data` > Schemas > `nyc` > Tables, and preview `taxi`. Sort a column. Convert to Code shows `FROM "sample_data"."nyc"."taxi"`. 5. Set the variable to an incorrect token, restart Positron, and connect. The error starts with "MotherDuck rejected the access token" and does not contain the token. 6. Install ggsql from the related PR. In the connection dialog, copy the ggsql code and run it in the ggsql console. Then run `SELECT count(*) FROM sample_data.nyc.taxi`.

title: Open browseURL() files in a new tab on Workbench
description:
Fixes #10893 Closes #10941 On Workbench, `browseURL()` of a local file did nothing. The `OpenWithSystem` runtime event built a `vscode-remote://` URI and passed it to the opener service with `openExternal`. On web, the default external opener only opens `http(s)` URLs in a new tab. Any other scheme is assigned to `window.location`, and Chromium logs `Failed to launch 'vscode-remote://...' because the scheme does not have a registered handler`. This PR adds `openRuntimeResourceWithSystem` in `mainThreadLanguageRuntime.ts`. On desktop it keeps the current behavior: the OS default application opens the file. On web it serves the file through the positron-proxy HTML proxy server and opens that URL externally. The Viewer's "Open in Browser" button already uses this path, so the opener service rewrites the localhost URL to the Workbench port proxy and the new tab is same-origin. The `/vscode-remote-resource` endpoint was not used. The server sends `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; sandbox` with it, so a rendered report would lose its CSS and JavaScript. ### Release Notes #### New Features - N/A #### Bug Fixes - Workbench: `browseURL()` on a local file now opens the file in a new browser tab (#10893) ### Validation Steps @:workbench The new Workbench e2e test, `test/e2e/tests/workbench/browse-url/browse-url.test.ts`, starts R, writes a small HTML file, calls `browseURL()` on it, and expects a new tab that shows the page heading. Without the fix, the test fails with a timeout while it waits for the new tab. Unit tests for the helper are in `mainThreadLanguageRuntime.vitest.ts`: ```bash npx vitest run src/vs/workbench/api/test/browser/positron/mainThreadLanguageRuntime.vitest.ts ``` Manual check on Workbench: 1. Start an R session. 2. Run: ```r html <- tempfile(fileext = ".html") writeLines("

Hello

", html) browseURL(html) ``` 3. A new browser tab opens and shows the heading. On desktop, the file opens in the default browser as before. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Report dpkg-shlibdeps download errors instead of running the error page
description:
The Linux daily build failed in the "Prepare Linux packages" step ([failed run](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron-builds/actions/runs/39740067194)). To work out the .deb package dependencies, the build downloads Chromium's `dpkg-shlibdeps.pl` script from `raw.githubusercontent.com`. GitHub answered with HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests). curl saved that error page as the script, so perl failed with a confusing error:

```
syntax error at /tmp/dpkg-shlibdeps.pl line 1, near "429:"
```

This PR changes the download in `build/linux/debian/calculate-deps.ts` in three ways:

- Fewer requests. The old code downloaded the script once for every binary it checked: each native module, the main executable, `chrome-sandbox`, and `chrome_crashpad_handler`. Now each build job downloads it once and reuses the file.
- Authenticated download in CI. When `GITHUB_TOKEN` is set, the script comes from the GitHub API with that token instead of anonymously from `raw.githubusercontent.com`. The positron-builds Linux job already sets `GITHUB_TOKEN`. Without the token the code uses the old URL.
- A clear error on failure. If the response is not HTTP 200, the build stops with the status code and GitHub's response text, and the script file is not written. If curl itself fails, the error includes curl's exit code and message.

The file comes from upstream, so the changes are inside Positron markers.

### Release Notes

- N/A

No e2e suite runs this code. It only runs when the Linux .deb is built.

title: Fix two flaky ext-host tests: Redshift expiry bound and Copilot activation deadlock
description:
Fixes two ext-host tests that were red on `main` this week: the Redshift IAM credentials test in the Electron step, and the six "Completions in settings.json" tests in the Remote step.

### Summary

**Redshift IAM credentials (test bug, 5 of the last 40 main merges).** The test `falls back to the requested lifetime when AWS reports no expiry` sampled the clock before the call, but the fallback expiry samples the clock inside the call. The measured lifetime was therefore 3600 s plus the call time, and the upper bound `<= 3600` only held when zero milliseconds elapsed. The test now brackets the expiry between `before + 1h` and `after + 1h`.

**Settings.json completions in the Remote step (product deadlock).** Every settings.json test timed out while the extensions.json, launch.json, tasks.json, and keybindings.json suites passed. The chain, confirmed with a local Remote reproduction and `--logExtensionHostCommunication`:

1. The JSON language server requests Copilot's `ccsettings://root/schema.json`, which the Copilot extension contributes as the schema for every `settings.json`.
2. Opening that document activates Copilot Chat on the `onFileSystem:ccsettings` event.
3. With no GitHub session, Copilot's `ConversationFeature` activation blocker never settles. The blocker waits for a BYOK model query. The window answers that query only after it activates the extension that provides the vendor, and that extension is Copilot itself. The `onDidAuthenticationChange` event that upstream relies on to break this loop fires only when the identity changes, which never happens without a session.
4. The document open, the schema, and every later settings.json completion wait forever.

The suite passed only when an earlier `onLanguageModelChatProvider:copilot` request had already started Copilot's activation, so its content provider was registered before the schema request. Upstream `main` carries the same code, so this is a marked Positron patch in a vendored file. The patch settles the blocker after the first Copilot token attempt completes, which is what the upstream comment above it already intends.

The same deadlock also leaves any `selectChatModels` call that touches a Copilot-provided vendor pending until the window closes when there is no Copilot sign-in. The shutdown lines in the failing job log show that for the copilot, anthropic, gemini, and openai vendors. This patch resolves that as well.

### Release Notes

#### New Features
- N/A

#### Bug Fixes
- Fix settings.json completions and language model queries hanging when Copilot Chat has no GitHub session.

### Validation Steps

@:assistant @:vscode-settings

Both ext-host jobs on this PR should be green. Locally:

1. `npm run test-extension -- -l positron-data-driver-redshift --grep "Redshift IAM Credentials"` passes.
2. The configuration-editing suite from `scripts/test-remote-integration.sh` passes with all 12 tests, including the six settings.json tests. Before the patch it reproduced the six timeouts on the first local run.
3. In the Remote ext host log, `activationBlocker from 'conversationFeature'` now reports a duration instead of never appearing.

title: e2e: stub native print in PDF print test to stop renderer hang
description:
### Summary Fixes the "PDF Viewer > Can print PDF file" e2e flake (7.8% on main, Linux chromium), where the test hung until its 120s timeout. - pdf.js calls the native `window.print()` as soon as print preparation hits 100% (~150ms after the click), which freezes the renderer on chromium; any Playwright call still pending in the PDF frame then hangs - The test now stubs `window.print` in the PDF viewer frame before the PDF opens, so the page stays responsive - It asserts the stub was called (pdf.js only calls print after preparing every page) instead of the transient "Preparing document" overlay - Trimmed redundant comments in the spec ### QA Notes @:pdf @:web ### E2E Triage Diagnosis
🟢 High confidence -- pdf.js calls the native window.print() once print preparation hits 100%, freezing the renderer on chromium; any Playwright call still pending in the PDF frame hangs until the test timeout - **Test:** [PDF Viewer > Can print PDF file](https://connect.posit.it/e2e-test-insights/?tab=test_health&repo=positron&test=PDF%20Viewer%20%3E%20Can%20print%20PDF%20file%7C%7C%7Ctest%2Fe2e%2Ftests%2Fpdf%2Fpdf.test.ts) - **Targeted failure:** Test timeout of 120000ms exceeded. - **Signal:** Same in 2 occurrences (ubuntu 13611e8, rhel 8dc805e): print click ok; the 'Preparing document' overlay goes 67% to 100% within ~150ms and freezes at 100% (pdf.js closes it only after native print returns); the toBeVisible expect started ~25ms after the click never returns, the screencast stops, and the failure Page.screenshot times out after 30s; no crash page, logs silent - **Frequency:** 12/153 runs (7.8%) on main, ubuntu/chromium, rhel/chromium, debian/chromium - **Hypothesis:** race

title: Choose which coding agent Fix and Explain send errors to
description:
Stacked on #16865. Part of #13603.

[LLM-generated walkthrough of user-facing changes with screenshots.](https://connect.posit.it/connect/#/apps/91890927-fc3e-4187-a17e-036dbafd0858/content-view). This is also on our QuartoHub, DM me for the link.

Adds `ai.errorActions.agent`, which picks the coding agent that console, notebook, and Quarto Fix/Explain send errors to. It defaults to Posit Assistant, so nothing changes until a user picks another, and nothing else can be picked yet: Claude Code doesn't register as a handler until a follow-up.

The choices are whichever handlers are registered, so a new agent only has to register to show up. If the chosen agent isn't available, the buttons still show, and clicking one explains why and offers to pick another (or, if an admin set it by policy, just says so).

Because the setting decides where error contents go, it's ignored in untrusted workspaces, and extensions can't set it through configuration defaults. It's machine-overridable because agents are installed per host.

Worth a look: the choices are added to the schema at runtime by editing its arrays in place, since the Settings editor caches them (`setErrorActionHandlerChoices`).

<!-- TODO: screenshots - (1) the "Error Actions: Agent" entry in the Settings editor with its dropdown open; (2) the "The coding agent 'claude-code' isn't available" notification with its "Select Another Coding Agent" button -->

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- N/A (the release note lands with the Claude Code handler)

#### Bug Fixes

- N/A

### Validation Steps

1. Open the Settings editor and search for `errorActions`. Check that "Error Actions: Agent" is listed, with Posit Assistant selected and as the only choice.
2. With Posit Assistant installed and a chat model signed in, run `stop("boom")` in an R console. Check that Fix and Explain appear and that Fix opens a Posit Assistant chat, as before.
3. In your user `settings.json`, set `"ai.errorActions.agent": "claude-code"`. In the Settings editor, check that the dropdown now shows "claude-code (not available)" rather than jumping back to Posit Assistant.
4. Run `stop("boom")` again and click Fix. Check that no chat opens, and that a notification says "The coding agent 'claude-code' isn't available, so the error wasn't sent." Click "Select Another Coding Agent" and check that it opens your user settings at `ai.errorActions.agent`.
5. Set the same value in a workspace `.vscode/settings.json` instead, then repeat step 4. Check that the button opens the workspace settings. Reopen the folder in Restricted Mode and check that the workspace value is ignored and Fix goes to Posit Assistant.
6. Remove the setting and sign out of every Posit Assistant model. Check that the Fix and Explain buttons disappear from the console, notebook, and Quarto errors.

title: Write the pinned interpreter over the affiliated runtime at startup
description:
Part 1 of 4 for #2659. Stack, bottom to top: #16849 (core) -> #16850 (R) -> #16838 (Python) -> #16851 (R file open). Each PR shows only its own commits. To try the whole feature, check out the top PR.

How it works, with diagrams of the startup sequence: [`plans/2659-how-it-works.md`](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/dhruvi/2659-pinned-interpreter-plan/plans/2659-how-it-works.md) in #16572. The Q numbers refer to the decisions doc, `plans/2659-pinned-interpreter.md`. The steps of the startup sequence: 1 reconnects running consoles, 2 starts the affiliated runtimes, 3 starts recommendations, 4 searches for interpreters, and 5 starts a runtime once the search ends.

## What this PR does

`python.defaultInterpreterPath` and `positron.r.interpreters.default` will set the interpreter that starts in a folder, in place of the one used last. The code calls it the pinned interpreter. This PR adds the core part.

Core gets a new optional runtime manager method, `pinnedWorkspaceRuntime()`. Right after a language's extension activates, core asks it for the pin and writes the pin over the language's affiliated runtime. So step 2 starts the pin.

No extension implements the method in this PR. Users see no change until #16850 (R) and #16838 (Python).

- Core waits at most 20 seconds for an answer. Python gives up on its own lookup after 15 seconds, so in practice the limit only catches an extension that hangs. On a timeout, the affiliated runtime starts as saved, and a late answer is still saved. The next launch asks again.
- A console in step 2 waits only for its own language's check.
- Step 4 waits for a check in one case only: no console is running, and the old affiliated runtime can still start as the cache registers it. When that check finds a pin, the pin starts there. On almost every launch, it does not wait.
- A new start reason, `pinnedRuntime`, tells the user that the pin started the interpreter.

## Commits

1. **Add `pinnedWorkspaceRuntime()` to the runtime manager API.** One pass-through at each layer. The extension host matches the manager by extension ID as well as language, because positron-python and positron-reticulate both register for `python`. A missing manager or a throw returns undefined (Q14). The extension host marks every answer `Implicit`, so an extension cannot make a pin start right away.
2. **Add a test helper that runs the runtime startup sequence.** Test only. It declares the `languageRuntimes` contributions, as an extension does, records each request to start an interpreter, and waits for step 5's answers. The first console that starts or reconnects counts as the console in front.
3. **Write the pinned interpreter over the affiliated runtime after activation.** The pinned check, once per language per window.
   - It keeps the old last-started and last-used times, so step 2 starts or skips the pin the same way as the old runtime.
   - It registers the pin, so the pin skips `validateMetadata()` at start and never reaches the discovery cache.
   - Under `definitionsOnly`, it writes the first matching `interpreters.definitions` entry (Q10).
   - It skips a language with no affiliated runtime, the language the New Folder flow just picked, and `recommended` (Q2, Q4, Q6, Q14).
   - It adds the 20-second limit and the step 4 rule above.
   - In step 4, it starts the pin itself. The check registers the pin before the cache or the search can, so their registration of it starts nothing.
4. **Show that a pinned interpreter started because it is pinned.** This adds the start reason `pinnedRuntime`. Its label: "Positron started the default {language} interpreter set in the {extension} extension's settings".
5. **Test how pinned interpreters start with remembered recommendations.** Core tests of #16728's behavior with a pin: file open, running code under `recommended`, and `[r]` set to `always`.

## Not in this PR

- A pin that starts through the recommendation shows the recommendation's start reason, not `pinnedRuntime`. That happens in a new folder and under `recommended`. Showing the pinned reason needs a new per-answer field in the recommendation API.
- On the first launch after the pin changes, the Console pane names the old interpreter until the check ends. It shows the saved interpreter before the extension activates, as on main, so every launch can name an interpreter early.

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- N/A

#### Bug Fixes

- N/A

### Validation Steps

@:interpreter @:sessions @:console @:critical

- Vitest: the startup sequence, including a pinned check that never answers, one that answers late, and a pin that starts when nothing started before the search. The extension host API. The `pinnedRuntime` start reason label.
- No extension reports a pin yet, so startup behaves as on main. #16850 and #16838 have the checks by hand.

description:
Part 2 of 4 for #2659. Stack, bottom to top: #16849 (core) -> #16850 (R) -> #16838 (Python) -> #16851 (R file open). Each PR shows only its own commits. To try the whole feature, check out the top PR.

Closes #16446. #16411 fixed item 1, #16728 fixed item 2, item 3 needed no change, #16445 tracks item 4, and this PR fixes item 5.

How it works: [`plans/2659-how-it-works.md`](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/dhruvi/2659-pinned-interpreter-plan/plans/2659-how-it-works.md) in #16572. The Q numbers refer to the decisions doc, `plans/2659-pinned-interpreter.md`.

## What this PR does

R implements #16849's `pinnedWorkspaceRuntime()`. So `positron.r.interpreters.default` now sets the R that starts in a folder, in place of the R used last. If you pick another R, your pick lasts until the next launch.

What changes for users:

- **The pinned R starts.** In a folder with an affiliated R, the pinned R starts in its place. In a folder without one, R's recommendation is the pinned R.
- **Both consoles start.** A pinned R now starts right away in a folder that looks like an R project. An unpinned R already did. So a folder with R and Python files starts both consoles. Before, only Python started. `default-r-interpreter.test.ts` now expects both.
- **R checks the folder for a pinned R too.** That check decides whether R starts right away (Q13). It takes up to 2 seconds, or about 4 seconds for RStudio users in an empty folder. Core waits for every language's recommendation before the first console. So on a launch where no console starts from the last session, a pinned R can delay the first console by that much. The pin lookup runs during the search, so it adds no time of its own.
- **CRAN's macOS R without rig.** R at `/usr/local/bin/R` now counts as the current R. Before, Positron rejected it as not usable. Registering it from a path now adds the current R once.
- **No saved R recommendation.** R no longer saves its recommendation as the affiliated runtime before it starts. So a pinned R in a folder with no R files no longer starts on the second open (Q13).

## Commits

6. **Follow symlinks in the current-R check.** `validateMetadata()` and `registerRuntimeFromPath()` use the new path comparison. A link to the current R registers at the current R's own path. `positron.r.customBinaries` keeps the path as you gave it.
7. **Report R's pinned interpreter to Positron.** R's `pinnedWorkspaceRuntime()`.
   - It returns nothing under `definitionsOnly`, for a missing path (Q9, with a warning in the log), or for an R that is not usable.
   - So `positron.r.interpreters.exclude` and `positron.r.interpreters.override` win over the pin (#16446 item 5). Their descriptions now say so.
   - A pin in a conda or pixi environment starts with it activated (Q12).
   - A pin that the r-versions file lists gets that entry's label, module, startup script, and library, as discovery builds them. R reads only the r-versions file for this, and skips entries with a module and no path.
   - On Windows, discovery lists R at `bin\x64\R.exe` where that file exists, and a pin at `bin\R.exe` maps to that path.
   - The decision is in `startup-choice.ts`, so Vitest can test it.
8. **Start a pinned R right away in R projects, and recommend an R after discovery.**
   - In an R project, the pinned R is `Immediate`. In other folders, and under `manual`, it is `Implicit` (Q13).
   - The pin lookup runs while R searches the folder, so the two times overlap.
   - Core can ask for the pinned check and the recommendation at once. They then share one running pin lookup. A finished lookup is never reused, so a changed setting is always read again.
   - R now answers core's second ask after discovery (`afterDiscovery`): the pinned R, or else the R it lists first. The answer comes from the Rs core already registered, so it never searches again. Commit 9 needs this: without it, `[r]` set to `always` starts nothing in a folder with no R files and no pin.
9. **Stop saving R's recommendation as the workspace's default.** R sets `recommendationIsProjectDefault: false`, as Python does (Q13).

## Not in this PR

- Opening an R file starts the first registered `Implicit` R. If the pinned R registers after another R, that other R starts. #16851 fixes this. Main behaves the same way.
- With CRAN's R and no rig, an `interpreters.definitions` entry for `/usr/local/bin/R` stays unusable, as on main. The fix needs `validateMetadata()` to keep a definition's exact path.

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- N/A. #16838 has the note for both settings.

#### Bug Fixes

- With CRAN's macOS R installer and no rig, R at `/usr/local/bin/R` is no longer rejected as not usable.

### Validation Steps

@:interpreter @:ark @:critical @:win

Automated:

- Vitest: R's decisions, R's path comparison.
- positron-r extension host tests: `R pinned runtime`, `R startup recommendation`, `R current R check`.

By hand:

- **R:** use R 4.3 in a folder, then set `positron.r.interpreters.default` to R 4.4 and reopen. R 4.4 starts. The console info popup says "Positron started the default R interpreter set in the R extension's settings".
- **R set to `manual`:** nothing starts. Run R code, and R 4.4 starts.
- **A path that does not exist:** the old affiliated R starts, and the R log warns about the path.
- **A pinned R in a folder with no R files:** R does not start on open. Open an R file or run R code, and the pinned R starts.
- **A pinned R in a folder with R and Python files:** both consoles start.
- **`[r]` set to `always`, no R files, no setting:** R starts.
- **macOS with CRAN's R installer and no rig:** set the R setting to `/usr/local/bin/R`, and that R starts.
- **Workbench with an r-versions entry for the pinned R:** the console starts with the entry's module and library, and the picker shows the entry's label.

title: On R file open, start R's recommendation, not the first discovered R
description:
Part 4 of 4 for #2659. Stack, bottom to top: #16849 (core) -> #16850 (R) -> #16838 (Python) -> #16851 (R file open). Each PR shows only its own commits. Check out this PR to try the whole feature.

Closes #16376. #16740 fixed R's search and #16728 fixed Python's search. This PR adds the last piece: the discovery cache never stores `Immediate`.

How it works: [`plans/2659-how-it-works.md`](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/dhruvi/2659-pinned-interpreter-plan/plans/2659-how-it-works.md) in #16572. Its startup flowchart and step table already show this PR's changes, in green.

## The case this fixes

Opening an R file can start the current R instead of the pinned R. It happens under three conditions:

- R has no affiliated runtime in the folder.
- Another language's console starts first, so step 3 does not ask R for a recommendation.
- Discovery registers the current R before the pinned R.

After discovery, R recommends the pinned R. But on file open, the session service starts the first registered `Implicit` R. Every discovered R is `Implicit`, and the current R comes first.

## What changes

- **Discovered Rs are `Explicit`, as for Python.** Only R's recommendation and the pinned R are `Implicit`. So no discovered R competes on file open.
- **File open starts the preferred runtime.** Running code starts the same one: the affiliated runtime, else the one started last, else the recommendation. If an `Implicit` runtime of the language is registered, core still leaves the start to the session service. Before, core also stood aside for any affiliated runtime. With discovered Rs `Explicit`, that left nothing to start an affiliated R that step 2 skipped. Python's discovered runtimes were already `Explicit`, so this also fixes the same case for Python.
- **R answers from its definitions.** Under `definitionsOnly`, R now recommends its first defined R after discovery. Before, it recommended nothing. With discovered Rs `Explicit`, opening an R file then starts no R.
- **Each language is asked as soon as its own search ends.** Before, core asked again only after every language finished. Now, at the end of each language's search, the extension host tells core, and core asks that language right away. A language the cache covers is asked once the cache loads. So an R file opened during Python's search starts R without waiting for Python. An `Immediate` answer still waits for every language, and the `always` start still runs once at the end.
- **The cache never stores `Immediate`.** Every folder shares the discovery cache, but whether an interpreter starts right away depends on the open folder. The cache now stores `Immediate` as `Implicit`, and the background recheck registers a changed record the same way. R and Python already leave `Immediate` off what their searches find, so this protects other language extensions. It is the core rule that #16740 promised for #16376.

What users notice:

- With a pin, opening an R file starts the pinned R in the case above.
- Without a pin, opening an R file starts the R that R lists first, as before.
- Step 2 skips an affiliated runtime that was not used since it last started. Opening a file of its language now starts it. That holds for R and Python.
- The first launch after this update runs a full search for every language, Python included. The discovery cache version goes from 4 to 5, which discards every cached interpreter once. Without the bump, cached Rs stay `Implicit` until their next full search.

## Commits

1. **Discovered Rs are `Explicit`, and file open starts the preferred runtime.** R marks discovered Rs `Explicit`, and the pin passes `Implicit`. Cache version 5. Core's file-open start uses the preferred runtime. Core tests for the case above, and for an affiliated R that step 2 skipped, opened after startup and during discovery.
2. **R's first defined R under `definitionsOnly`.** R reports no pinned R in that mode.
3. **Each language asked after its own search.** The extension host has a new call, `$completeLanguageRuntimeDiscoveryForLanguage(languageId)`. It sends the call once every manager for that language is done. Core asks each language at most once per discovery pass.
4. **The cache never stores `Immediate`.** A new helper, `cachedRuntimeMetadata()` in `runtimeDiscoveryCacheService.ts`. The cache's `upsert()` and the background recheck both use it. Tests: a record saved as `Immediate` reads back as `Implicit`, and a drifted record the recheck registers is `Implicit`.

## Not in this PR

- The session service's "first `Implicit` runtime" file-open start stays. No built-in language relies on it now, but third-party language extensions can.
- To ask a language early, core needs to know which languages each extension host searches. Three cases fall back to waiting for every language: the discovery cache is off, you run Discover All Interpreters, or an extension host does not list its languages.

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- N/A

#### Bug Fixes

- Opening an R or Python file now starts the interpreter used in the folder before, after Positron skipped it at startup.

### Validation Steps

@:interpreter @:ark @:critical

Automated:

- Vitest: the startup sequence and the extension host API.
- positron-r extension host tests: `R pinned runtime`, `R startup recommendation`.
- E2E: `pinned-interpreter.test.ts` and `r-startup-cached.test.ts` pass locally. `default-r-interpreter.test.ts` needs the hidden R from the CI image, so CI covers it.

By hand, with R and Python installed:

1. In a folder with a `.py` file and no R files, set `positron.r.interpreters.default` to an R that is not the current R. Open the `.py` file, and run Python code once so Python is the interpreter used last. Close the window.
2. Reopen the folder. Python starts. Open or create an `.R` file. The pinned R starts, not the current R.
3. Run Developer: Reload Window with the `.R` file still open. The pinned R starts once R's search ends.
4. Clear `positron.r.interpreters.default` and repeat step 2. The current R starts, as on main.
5. Set `interpreters.discovery` to `definitionsOnly` with two R entries in `interpreters.definitions`. Open an `.R` file in a folder with no affiliated R. The R from the first R entry starts.

title: ci: paginate PR comments when finding the e2e tags comment
description:
Fixes #16783

`scripts/pr-e2e-comment.sh` now fetches PR comments with `gh api --paginate`. Before, it read only the first 30 comments. If the tags comment was past page 1, the script posted a second one and did not delete duplicates.

The test commit adds a check to `scripts/test/pr-tags-lib-test.sh`, which CI already runs. A fake `gh` returns 30 unrelated comments on page 1 and the tags comment plus a duplicate on page 2. I could not run the shell test in this job, because the sandbox blocked `bash` scripts. CI runs it in the "Unit test the tag-derivation helpers" step. Without the fix, the three `comment:` checks fail, because the script posts a new comment.

title: Environment Modules: run `module purge` before `module load`
description:
Fixes #14744

### Summary

Adds an optional `purge` field to each entry in `positron.environmentModules.environments`. It defaults to `true`.

When `purge` is on and the module system is Lmod or Environment Modules, Positron runs `module purge` before `module load`. This applies to the kernel startup command and to interpreter discovery, so the discovered interpreter matches the one the session runs. Purge does not run on an `unknown` module system.

```json
"positron.environmentModules.environments": {
  "R 4 Stable": {
    "languages": ["r"],
    "modules": ["R/4.4.2"],
    "purge": false
  }
}
```

Notes:
- Entries from the `r-versions` file have no config entry, so they do not purge. Their behavior does not change.
- The terminal environment capture does not purge. It applies module changes as a diff on top of the terminal's own environment, and a purge cannot be expressed as such a diff.
- The diagnostics report now shows the purge value for each environment.

### Release Notes

#### New Features
- Environment Modules: R and Python sessions now run `module purge` before loading modules. Set `"purge": false` on an environment to keep modules from shell startup scripts (#14744)

#### Bug Fixes
- N/A

### Validation Steps

@:environment-modules

1. On a Linux host with Lmod or Environment Modules, load a module in `~/.bashrc`.
2. Configure an environment with no `purge` field. Start a session for it.
3. Run `Sys.getenv("LOADEDMODULES")` (R) or `os.environ["LOADEDMODULES"]` (Python). Only the configured modules appear.
4. Set `"purge": false`, refresh interpreters, and start a new session. The module from `~/.bashrc` also appears.

New Mocha unit tests are in `extensions/positron-environment-modules/src/test/module-system.test.ts`. I could not run them in this job, because the extension host is not available. The extension compiles with `npm run compile`.

title: Viewer agent press: do the key's default action, or say it won't happen
description:
Fixes #16743

`positronViewer.press` sent synthetic `keydown`/`keyup` events and reported success. Browsers never run a key's default action for script-created events, so Enter in a search box told the agent `Pressed Enter in the textbox "Query".` while the form never submitted.

`press` still sends the events, since page key handlers rely on them. Now, when the page doesn't cancel the key, it also does what the browser would:

- **Enter in a text box:** clicks the form's first submit button (so the button's own click handlers run and the form is validated), or submits a form with one text box and no button (implicit submission). If the form doesn't submit, the message says why: the button is disabled, or a field is empty or invalid.
- **Enter or Space on a button, Enter on a link:** clicks it.
- **Space on a checkbox or radio button:** toggles it, and checks that it changed, as `click` does.
- **ArrowUp or ArrowDown in a number box:** steps it (by 1 with `step="any"`), then fires `input` and `change`.
- **Any other key:** no longer claims success. It says the page's handlers got the key but the browser won't act on it, and suggests `fill`, `select` or `click`.

The `positronViewer.press` description, which the positron-commands skill reference includes, now lists the keys that do something.

### Notes for reviewers

- For `press` only, `pressKey` also sends `keypress` for Enter and character keys (skipped when `keydown` is cancelled, as browsers do), and sets the legacy `keyCode`/`which`/`charCode` on its key events. Chromium runs Enter's default action on `keypress`, so a page that cancels Enter there (an older jQuery pattern) keeps its form. The slider, select and Escape code that also calls `pressKey` sends the same plain `keydown`/`keyup` as before.
- Desktop could send trusted input through Electron instead, but the web build has no equivalent, so this emulates the default actions in the bridge for both.
- The Vitest cases run in happy-dom, which differs from browsers in three places the code handles: it includes image buttons in `form.elements`, lets `stepUp()` run with `step="any"`, and doesn't match buttons in a disabled fieldset with `:disabled`. Those three paths have no tests, since happy-dom can't fail them.

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- N/A

#### Bug Fixes

- Assistant's Viewer `press` command now submits a form on Enter, steps number boxes and toggles checkboxes, and no longer reports success for keys the browser won't act on (#16743)


### Validation Steps

@:viewer

1. Run the snippet from #16743 in a Python console, so the search form shows in the Viewer.
2. With Posit Assistant, ask it to search for "moons" by pressing Enter in the Query box. The page should read `Searched for moons`, and `press` should answer `Pressed Enter in the textbox "Query", which submitted its form.`
3. In a Shiny app with a `numericInput` and a `checkbox`, ask Assistant to press ArrowUp in the number box and Space on the checkbox. The server's output should update for both.
4. Ask it to press Escape in a text box. The answer should say the browser won't act on the key, not that it was pressed successfully.

title: e2e: Create Environment from the palette, then the Console
description:
Closes #14350

### Summary

Adds Playwright tests for `Python: Create Environment...` run from the command palette. The positron-python unit tests cover the provider flow itself. These tests cover what those cannot: Positron registers the new environment in the session picker without "Discover All Interpreters", and the Console starts it.

Three files in `test/e2e/tests/interpreters/`, each in its own worker:

- `create-environment-venv.test.ts`: create a venv from the palette; "Use Existing" keeps the running console; "Delete and Recreate" starts a fresh console and the picker still lists the venv once.
- `create-environment-conda.test.ts`: create a conda env and start it. Skips when conda is not installed.
- `create-environment-no-folder.test.ts`: close the folder, accept the global environment modal, and start the uv env created under a temp `WORKON_HOME`. Skips when uv is not installed.

Notes for reviewers:

- The venv test picks the first base interpreter the picker offers. The picker never offers pyenv Pythons: the extension types pyenv as a virtual environment, and the venv provider only accepts non-virtual interpreters. So `POSITRON_PY_ALT_VER_SEL` cannot be picked there. A venv built on a uv-managed base is classified as uv, so the "started" check accepts `Venv` or `uv`.
- The tests open their workspace by its resolved path. On macOS `$TMPDIR` goes through `/var` -> `/private/var`, and Positron registers an environment created under the symlink spelling twice. CI runners have no such symlink. The duplicate registration is tracked in #16861.
- The no-folder test is not tagged for the web lane. `extraEnv` only reaches the Electron process, so on the web project `WORKON_HOME` is unset and the modal offers `~/.virtualenvs/positron` on the runner.
- The test workspaces live beside the shared e2e workspace (`$TMPDIR/vscsmoke/create-env/`), not inside it. The first CI round put them inside `test-files`, and the leftover venv, built on the primary Python, outranked the global interpreter in later notebook tests' kernel pickers (the inline data explorer tests failed on both lanes with `import pandas` in a bare venv).

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- N/A

#### Bug Fixes

- N/A

### Validation Steps

@:interpreter @:python @:web

All three files pass locally on e2e-electron. The venv and conda files also pass on e2e-chromium.

title: Supporting changes for move to standalone core compile job
description:
Positron changes needed by posit-dev/positron-builds#1321, which moves release builds to the upstream `gulp core-ci` + `*-min-ci` pipeline (the "optional alternative" in #16466). See that PR for the background, results, and test runs.

Fixes #16466.

### Summary

- **Wait for extension binaries to finish copying.** The `copy-extension-binaries` task started the copy but returned before it finished. The new pipeline runs this task on its own, so it has to complete before packaging starts. Gulp now keeps the file mode on copy, so the separate step that restored the executable bit is gone.
- **Install linked extensions one at a time.** `postinstall` installs dirs that depend on each other through `file:` links in order, one at a time, instead of in parallel. In parallel, one dir's `prepare` compile could read files another was still writing, which caused random `npm ci` failures.
- **Drop an unused copy of the web workbench.** The esbuild server-web bundle no longer emits `workbench.web.main.internal` as its own entry point. It is already bundled into `workbench.js`, and nothing loads the separate copy (about 28 MB with CSS and gzip).
- **Go back to the upstream heap size.** The gulp heap limit returns to 8 GB, since no release build uses the in-process TypeScript compiler anymore.

### Merge orchestration

The two PRs depend on each other, so they need to land in this order:

1. **Merge this PR first.** 
2. **Update positron-builds#1321** to pin the `positron` submodule to the merge commit of this PR on `main` (it currently pins a commit on this branch), then merge it.

Do this promptly. Until positron-builds#1321 merges, the old pipeline still compiles the Linux server builds with the in-process compiler, which needs more than 8 GB of heap. If the submodule moves to a `main` commit that includes this PR (for example, via a dependabot bump) before positron-builds#1321 merges, those builds will run out of memory.

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- N/A

#### Bug Fixes

- N/A

### Validation Steps

@:critical

These are build-only changes. They were tested by the full release build and e2e runs linked in positron-builds#1321. Locally, `npm ci` and `npm run gulp -- copy-extension-binaries` should succeed.

title: drive-positron: make the helpers and check.ts work on Windows
description:
Makes the drive-positron skill's helpers and its static checks work on Windows (Git Bash). I found these while testing a Viewer fix (#16743) by hand on Windows 11. Every helper's `--help` crashed, and `launch.sh` could not open Positron on a workspace folder.

### Summary

**Helpers (`scripts/`)**

- **`--help` crashed with ENOENT on a `C:\C:\...` path.** `dp-lib.ts` took its own folder from `new URL(import.meta.url).pathname`, which is `/C:/...` on Windows. It now uses `fileURLToPath`, which also handles a path with a space on macOS and Linux. The same line is fixed in `test/` and `heal/`.
- **`launch.sh -- --folder-uri file:///C:/... --log debug` never opened a window.** The launcher exited before CDP came up, with an empty log. Electron's Windows entry point exits with -1, before it logs anything, when an argument that looks like a URL (a scheme and a colon) has any other argument after it, short of `--`. This is its guard for CVE-2018-1000006. I confirmed it with a stub Electron app: `--folder-uri file:///C:/x` alone runs, and adding `--log debug` after it makes Electron exit. `scripts/code.bat` was not involved.
  - `launch.sh` now passes `--folder-uri` and `--file-uri` together with their values, as `--folder-uri=URL`, which Positron's argv parser (minimist) reads the same way.
  - On Windows, any other URL with arguments after it gets a usage error that says why, instead of a silent exit.
  - It only joins a value that doesn't start with `-`. In `--folder-uri --log debug`, `--folder-uri` is passed on as it was, for the app to report.
  - A URL right before a `--` is refused too, because the app reads everything after `--` as file names.
  - This logic lives in `join_uri_args()`, and the new `test/launch-args.test.ts` runs that function alone in bash. `check.ts`'s unit check picks it up.
- **`dp.ts` page commands then failed on Windows.**
  - `execFileSync` cannot start the `node_modules/.bin/playwright-cli` shell shim (ENOENT), so the helpers now run `@playwright/cli`'s own script with Node.
  - The `run-code` source (page-lib plus selectors) is longer than Windows' 32K command-line limit (ENAMETOOLONG). On Windows it now goes through a temp file with `run-code --filename`.

- **`open-file.sh` opened the right file on Windows, then refused it.** The tab's path reads `C:\Users\...\hello.R` and the workspace URI reads `/c:/Users/...`, so the two never matched. Both are now compared with `/` separators and a lowercase drive letter. `lib.pick`'s folder match had the same problem: Quick Open shows a folder as `sub\deep`, so `open-file.sh sub/deep/hello.R` matched no row.

**Checks (`test/check.ts`)**

On Windows, 6 of its 8 checks failed. All 8 now pass.

- **types, lint:** run `@typescript/native`'s tsc (what `.bin/tsc` points to) and eslint's bin script with Node, in place of the `.bin` shims.
- **help, pagefn, drift:** accept `\` path separators.
  - help: the `dp-*.ts` file filter, and `import()` through `pathToFileURL`.
  - pagefn: the compiler-host lookup of the planted self-test file.
  - drift: the folder prefixes it searches. Before this fix, selectors that exist in the source, like `.selected`, were reported as MISSING.
- **unit:** `heal/affected.ts` `readGraph` reads scripts as LF, so its `\n` patterns match a CRLF checkout.

**Smoke fixture (`test/fixture-app.ts`, `test/smoke.ts`)**

- These ran the `.bin/playwright-cli` shim (ENOENT on Windows). They now call `playwrightCli()`, which `dp-lib.ts` exports.
- The fixture's workspace URI was built as `` `file://${ws}` ``, which on Windows is `file://C:\...`: a host name and no path. It now uses `pathToFileURL(ws).href`.

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- N/A

#### Bug Fixes

- N/A (developer tooling only)

### Validation Steps

@:critical

No product code changes. Checked on Windows 11 (Git Bash):

1. `bash .claude/skills/drive-positron/scripts/viewer.sh --help` prints the header. I checked all 30 `.sh` helpers.
2. `launch.sh -- --folder-uri "file:///$(cygpath -m /tmp/ws)" --log debug` opens a window on the folder.
   - `playwright-cli attach` works.
   - `panel.sh editors` and `tree.sh --view Explorer rows` show the folder's file.
   - `stop.sh --cdp-port N --run-dir DIR` stops the window and removes the run directory, with no stray `Positron.exe`.
3. `node .claude/skills/drive-positron/test/check.ts` passes all 8 checks. A planted type error makes `types` fail, so the passes are real.
4. `node --test .claude/skills/drive-positron/test/launch-args.test.ts` passes 7 of 7. It fails when the join is broken back to two separate arguments.
5. What `launchFixture` does, run on its own: a workspace URI from `pathToFileURL`, `launch.sh`, then attach, resize and close through `playwrightCli()`, then `stop.sh`. The folder opened, and every step exited 0.

Not run:

- `test/smoke.ts` itself on Windows. Its `SMOKE_ROOT` is hardcoded to `/private/tmp/...`, and its fixture links a positron-python `.venv` that this checkout doesn't have, so it isn't runnable on Windows yet.
- Anything on macOS or Linux. The changes accept both path separators and both line endings, and `--folder-uri=URL` parses the same as the two-argument form. The nightly drive-positron workflow (Ubuntu) runs smoke against these helpers.

title: Show item counts on Data Connections group rows
description:
Fixes #14630

Group rows in the Data Connections pane now show how many items they hold, in parentheses after the name: "Tables (14)", "Views (3)", "Schemas (2)". The count is muted so the name stays what the eye lands on.

### When a count appears

- **Once a group has been expanded**, its count comes from the rows it loaded, and stays when the group is collapsed again.
- **Before a group is expanded**, a count appears when it is known without a query of its own:
  - the children the tree's existing look-ahead already fetched (Schemas, Databases, Catalogs and Views groups that keep their own row), or
  - a count the driver sends with the group, through the new optional `childCount` field (below).
- **No count** is shown for a group whose listing failed (it shows its error instead), or for one nothing is known about yet.
- Notice rows (such as "only the first N files were listed") are not counted.

### Driver counts before expansion

A new optional `childCount` field on `positron.DataConnectionNode` lets a driver say how many children a node has when it knows without fetching them. The extension host passes it on only when it is a non-negative integer, and extensions that browse connections through the API see it too. Drivers fill it where it is free or cheap:

- **ODBC:** Catalogs, Schemas, Tables and Views, from the one cached `SQLTables` listing the driver already holds.
- **Snowflake:** semantic view member groups (Logical Tables, Dimensions, Metrics, etc.), from the `DESCRIBE SEMANTIC VIEW` result already in hand.
- **SQLite, DuckDB, PostgreSQL, Redshift (both modes):** Tables and Views, from one count query per schema (or per database for SQLite) using the same filters as the listings. If the count query fails, the groups appear without counts and the schema still opens.

The groups keep their own listing query on expand rather than sharing one listing fetched by the parent, so a Refresh on a group that was never opened still returns fresh data. A Views group whose driver reports 0 is dropped without running the look-ahead query.

### Intentionally not included

- **The "1 of 14" label on each nested item from the issue's acceptance criteria.** Group rows now carry "(n)" meaning "how many this holds", so "bikes (1 of 6)" on a table row would read as a count of the table's own contents. An alphabetical position also carries little information once the group shows its total, and no database tool we know of labels rows this way. Happy to add it, inline or as a tooltip, if it turns out to be wanted.
- **Columns and Indexes counts before expansion.** These would need a query on every table expand, so they count after expanding as before.
- **Snowflake Tables/Views/Stages, Databricks and Pins** send no counts before expansion; each would need an extra remote round trip per group.

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- Data Connections group rows (Tables, Views, Schemas and others) now show how many items they hold, such as "Tables (14)", and for most drivers show it before the group is expanded (#14630).

#### Bug Fixes

- N/A

### Validation Steps

@:connections

1. Connect to a DuckDB or SQLite database that has tables and views. Before expanding anything below the connection or schema, the Tables and Views rows read "Tables (n)" and "Views (n)".
2. Expand Tables; the count matches the rows listed. Collapse it; the count stays.
3. Connect to a PostgreSQL database and expand a schema; Tables and Views show counts before being expanded.
4. Expand a table; Columns and Indexes show no count until expanded, then show one.
5. On a schema with no views, there is no Views row, as before.
6. Refresh a connection after adding a table; the Tables count updates.

Unit tests cover the tree's counting (driver count, look-ahead count, loaded count, notices, failed listings, refresh), the extension host's validation of `childCount`, and each driver's counts. The PostgreSQL and Redshift count queries are tested against mocked clients only, not a live server.

title: Be more surgical in falling back to Workbench session-specific URLs for static assets
description:
So that our own oft-used daily build environments get the same performance benefits of production, we'd like the `href` used to load Positron's `workbench.js` file and etc to use the shared path all Posit Workbench sessions use whenever possible. This enables browser caching and pre-fetching of these assets.

The only real case it sounds like where this is unsafe is if the Positron Preview Workbench option is in use. So, starting with 2026.11, if and only if that is the case, Workbench will put `POSITRON_WORKBENCH_STATIC_COMMIT` on the job. In this change, we start writing the shared `href` in almost all cases -- unless we're 2026.11+ _and_ there is a `POSITRON_WORKBENCH_STATIC_COMMIT` _and_ it doesn't match our local product.json.

#### New Features

I wasn't shouting this from the rooftops since it only affects behavior of daily builds.

title: python: drop support for Python 3.9 sessions
description:
Fixes #10698. Python 3.9 reached end-of-life over a year ago. This PR makes Python 3.10 the minimum supported version, which is also EOL, but will remain supported for now.

### Summary

- Python 3.9 interpreters are shown as "Unsupported", like 3.8 and older. They're sorted last, they aren't recommended, and Positron doesn't bundle ipykernel for them.
- New uv and conda environments don't offer Python 3.9.
- CI tests the oldest version on 3.10 now.
- The minimum-dependencies test and the kernel test project now use Python 3.10.
- The Python kernel no longer has fallbacks that only 3.9 needed, such as the check for a missing `importlib.metadata.packages_distributions`.

This PR _doesn't_ regenerate the bundled ipykernel requirements. I will do this in #16750 during monthly maintenance. Until then, the current bundled versions (ipykernel 6.31.0, IPython 8.18.1) work on 3.10 and later.

The docs on the Positron website need a separate update which I'll open but we probably won't merge until release time.

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- N/A

#### Bug Fixes

- Python 3.9 is no longer supported (#10698).

### Validation Steps

@:interpreter @:sessions @:help @:new-folder-flow

- With Python 3.9 installed, open the interpreter picker. Make sure that 3.9 shows as "Unsupported" and is listed after the supported versions. It may or may not work to start a session.
- Make sure that Python 3.10 and later sessions start with the bundled ipykernel and work as before.
- Make sure the "create a venv"/"install python" workflows don't offer 3.9.

title: Support environment modules in interpreter definitions
description:
Fixes #16585

### Summary

Interpreter definitions could not use Environment Modules. The startup script was sourced with `/bin/sh`, which is `dash` on Debian and Ubuntu. `dash` does not see the `module` shell function, so a script that called `module load` failed and the session did not start. Bash-only syntax such as `source` and `[[ ]]` failed for the same reason.

This PR changes how the startup script runs:

- The script is now sourced with bash (falling back to `/bin/sh` if bash is missing).
- Before the script runs, the module system's init script is sourced, so `module` is always defined. The init script comes from the environment modules extension, the same way r-versions entries load modules.

It also adds an optional `modules` field to interpreter definitions. It lists modules to load, in order, before the startup script runs, much like the `Module` and `Script` fields in r-versions. The variables the modules set are applied to the interpreter and to terminals, just like the ones the startup script sets. Like startup scripts, modules are skipped on Windows.

```json
"interpreters.definitions": [
  {
    "language": "r",
    "path": "/opt/R/4.6.0/bin/R",
    "label": "R 4.6.0 (modules)",
    "modules": ["R/4.6.0"],
    "startupScript": "~/setup.sh"
  }
]
```

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- Interpreter definitions can list environment modules to load with the new `modules` field (#16585)

#### Bug Fixes

- Interpreter definition startup scripts can now use `module load` and bash syntax (#16585)

### Validation Steps

@:interpreter @:environment-modules @:sessions

No e2e test covers interpreter definitions yet. The supervisor's extension tests cover the new ordering (module init, then modules, then the startup script) and bash syntax.

On Linux with Environment Modules or Lmod set up:

1. Create `~/load-modules.sh` with `module load <some R module>`.
2. Add an interpreter definition with `"startupScript": "~/load-modules.sh"`, and another with `"modules": ["<some R module>"]`.
3. Start each one and run `Sys.getenv(c("LOADEDMODULES", "R_HOME", "PATH"))`. The module's values should be there.
4. Add a definition with a module that does not exist. The session should fail to start and show the module system's error.

title: e2e: match Open Folder rows by exact option name in the openFolder fixture
description:
Fixes the `R - Verify can open, test, check, install, and restart package` failure in https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/actions/runs/39942576564 (strict mode violation in the `openFolder` fixture). ### Summary The `openFolder` fixture located the next folder row in the Open Folder quick pick with `getByText(folderName)`. That is a substring match over all text in the row, including text that is hidden. Quick-pick rows are recycled between pickers. The upstream row renderer hides the detail label when the next item has no detail, but it does not clear the old text. On the failing shard, `python-venv-creation` ran earlier in the same worker, so the session picker that the R package test opens in `beforeAll` listed the interpreter `/tmp/vscsmoke/test-files/venv-creation-test/.venv/bin/python`. The Open Folder list then reused that row. The hidden detail text still contained `test-files`, so the locator resolved to the hidden span, and then to two elements when the real `test-files` row scrolled into view. The fixture now matches the row by its exact accessible name: `quickInputList.getByRole('option', { name: folderName, exact: true })`. For file-dialog items the row `aria-label` is the bare folder name, so hidden detail text no longer matches. The stale hidden text is not visible to users, and the renderer is an upstream file, so there is no product change. ### Release Notes #### New Features - N/A #### Bug Fixes - N/A ### Validation Steps @:r-pkg-development @:interpreter @:packages-pane @:references @:sessions @:layouts @:test-explorer These suites cover every test that calls `openFolder`. Locally, `python-venv-creation` followed by `r-pkg-development` in one worker (the CI order) passed with the fix. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ### E2E Triage Diagnosis
🟢 High confidence -- openFolder fixture matches folder rows by substring text, which also matches hidden stale detail text left in recycled quick-pick rows by the earlier interpreter picker - **Test:** [R Package Development > R - Verify can open, test, check, install, and restart package](https://connect.posit.it/e2e-test-insights/?tab=test_health&repo=positron&test=R%20Package%20Development%20%3E%20R%20-%20Verify%20can%20open%2C%20test%2C%20check%2C%20install%2C%20and%20restart%20package%7C%7C%7Ctest%2Fe2e%2Ftests%2Fr-pkg-development%2Fr-pkg-development.test.ts) - **Targeted failure:** strict mode violation / hidden: .quick-input-widget .quick-input-list .monaco-list-row >> getByText('test-files') resolves to a hidden span '/tmp/vscsmoke/test-files/venv-creation-test/.venv/bin/python' inside a d-* folder row - **Signal:** Trace DOM snapshot at the failing expect: one quick-input widget titled Open Folder; row idx 9 (aria-label d-3e0bb5cl) carries a display:none .monaco-icon-label whose text is the venv interpreter path; rows 9-18 carry other interpreter paths and a hidden 'Suggested' separator. quickInputList.ts renderElement hides data.detail but never clears its label when the new item has no detail (upstream file). python-venv-creation ran earlier on the same worker (shard electron-1, test 152 vs 288), so that interpreter was in the session picker the fixture opened in beforeAll. - **Frequency:** 2/134 runs (1.5%) on main, ubuntu/electron - **Hypothesis:** Recycled monaco-list row templates keep the previous picker's detail text hidden in the DOM. getByText is a substring match over all text in the row, so a folder name that is a substring of any stale interpreter path (test-files appears in the venv-creation-test venv path) resolves to the hidden span, then to two elements once the real row scrolls into view. Ruled out: a second quick-input widget (exactly one in the snapshot), a dialog listing a stale entry (dialog labels are basenames only), timing (first expect failed before any PageDown and the retry attempt failed identically).

title: Send Fix and Explain errors to Claude Code
description:
Stacked on #16866.

Fixes #13603

Claude Code can now be chosen in `ai.errorActions.agent` while its extension or its `claude` command is installed. Each Fix or Explain then opens a new Claude Code conversation, in its chat panel with the prompt filled in or in a terminal per Claude Code's Use Terminal setting, with a prompt that stands on its own: where the error came from, the code, and the error. Other extensions can add coding agents with `positron.ai.registerErrorActionHandler` (proposed API `positronErrorActions`), declaring them in the `errorActionHandlers` contribution point so Positron can name and activate them before they register.

<!-- TODO: screen recording - choose Claude Code in Settings, click Fix on an R console error and show the Claude Code chat opening with the prompt filled in; then turn on Claude Code: Use Terminal and show Fix opening a Claude Code terminal running the prompt -->

### Release Notes

#### New Features

- Fix and Explain on console, notebook, and Quarto errors can send the error to Claude Code, chosen with the `ai.errorActions.agent` setting (#13603)

#### Bug Fixes

- N/A

### Validation Steps

1. Install the Claude Code extension (2.0.35 or later). Open the Settings editor, search for `errorActions`, and check that "Error Actions: Agent" lists Posit Assistant and Claude Code. Choose Claude Code.
2. In an R console, run `stop("boom")` and click Fix. Check that a new Claude Code chat opens with a prompt naming the console session, the code (`stop("boom")`), and the error, ending with "Fix the error. Only edit project files if the cause is in one of them." The prompt is filled in but not sent; send it yourself.
3. Click Explain on the same error. Check that the prompt asks it to explain without changing files. Check that Fix and Explain have no "in current chat" dropdown.
4. In a saved notebook, add a markdown cell and then a Python cell with `1/0`, and run it. Make an unsaved edit to the notebook and click Fix. Check that the prompt says "Cell 2 of /absolute/path/to/notebook.ipynb raised an error.", says the file has unsaved changes, and includes the cell's current code.
5. Repeat with an untitled notebook. Check that the prompt names it as a notebook that isn't saved to a file.
6. In a Quarto document, run a chunk that errors and click Fix. Check that the prompt names the chunk's language and lines and labels the code as "the chunk as run".
7. Turn on `claudeCode.useTerminal` and click Fix again. Check that a Claude Code terminal opens beside the editor and starts working on the prompt right away. If you're on Windows, also try an error with quotes, backslashes, and several lines.
8. With Use Terminal still on, take `claude` off your PATH (or test on a machine without it) and reload. Click Fix. Check that a warning says the claude command wasn't found and offers Open Settings, and that nothing opens.
9. Disable the Claude Code extension, keep `claude` off the PATH, and reload. Check that the Fix and Explain buttons still show, and that a click says "The coding agent 'Claude Code' isn't available, so the error wasn't sent. It may not be installed." with "Select Another Coding Agent". In Settings, check that the dropdown shows "Claude Code (not available)".
10. Turn off `ai.enabled`. Check that the Fix and Explain buttons disappear everywhere.

title: drive-positron: fix ui.sh and code every helper shares from the nightly run
description:
### Summary

Nightly self-heal: 2 helpers fixed, 1 fix rejected, ready to review.

**To do:** Review and merge this PR.

#### finder-choose-settings-dropdown: fixed

- **What broke:** `ui.sh choose` could not pick a value from a Settings drop-down, saying nothing opened, and `ui.sh read menu` said no menu was open.
- **Why:** The helpers did not recognise the select box's drop-down list as a menu, and remembered it as already open after it had been closed.
- **In a real run:** the agent did it by hand: 11:27:29Z ui.sh: FAILED choose combobox ai.errorActions.agent 'Posit Assistant' --in dialog: no menu, popup or list opened after clicking combobox "ai.errorActions.agent" | 11:27:33Z ui.sh: FAILED read menu: no menu is open | 11:27:34Z ui.sh: FAILED click option 'Posit Assistant': no visible option ...
- **Fix:** They now treat the drop-down as a menu, match its options by value, and only treat a list as already open if it was open just before this click.
- **Checked:** failed 3 of 3 tries before the fix; check.ts and all of smoke pass with it.

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

**Reason:** Helper bug, two causes on the same path. (1) The Settings editor's enum settings use upstream VS Code's SelectBoxList (src/vs/base/browser/ui/selectBox/selectBoxCustom.ts, file-origin.sh: upstream, no Positron block). It draws its drop-down as .monaco-select-box-dropdown-container, a [role=listbox] of [role=option] rows, in the workbench .context-view outside the Settings dialog. selectors.ts overlay.menu did not match it, so lib.opened (fresh(menu)) never saw it, and its inline-list search only looks under the trigger's dialog; lib.menu() (ui.sh read menu, --in menu, closeMenu, onTop) missed it too. Fix: overlay.menu now includes .monaco-select-box-dropdown-container; listIn already reads [role=option] rows and closeMenu's Escape applies because focus is in .context-view. Its options are named 'value. description' ('afterDelay. An editor with changes ...', 'off. default. ...'), which lib.choose's three name rules rejected, so lib.choose gets a fourth rule, tried last: a name that starts with 'item. '. (2) Found while checking the fix: after a ui.sh click or choose ran while the list was open, every later choose on that select box failed again with 'no menu, popup or list opened'. lib.markOverlays marked the open container data-dp-seen; the click closed it, which detaches the element, so the next markOverlays clean-up (document query) could not reach it, and SelectBoxList reattaches the same element on the next open, still marked, so lib.opened called it not new. Fix: each ma...

**Tries:**
- finder, fail: no menu, popup or list opened after clicking combobox "files.autoSave"; dropdown visible, value still off
- finder, fail: no menu, popup or list opened after clicking combobox "files.autoSave"; dropdown visible, value still off
- fixer, fail: palette-run 'Preferences: Open User Settings' then ui.sh choose combobox files.autoSave afterDelay --in dialog exited 1 with 'no menu, popup or list opened after clicking combobox "files.autoSave"' while the drop-down was open (.monaco-select-box-dropdown-container inside .context-view, listbox file...

**To reproduce:**

```sh
palette-run.sh --session heal-find 'Preferences: Open User Settings'
ui.sh --session heal-find choose combobox files.autoSave afterDelay --in dialog
shot.sh --session heal-find f1.png
ui.sh --session heal-find read menu
```

**Commit:** f86b4d4e368242ff7f466463adc4516e013a3829

</details>

#### finder-pick-row-under-hover: fixed

- **What broke:** `ui.sh pick` could not choose a quick pick row when the row above showed its tooltip over it; the click never landed.
- **Why:** It always clicked the middle of the row, which the tooltip of the row under the resting pointer covered.
- **In a real run:** the agent did it by hand: 18:35:32Z ui.sh: FAILED pick Venv: the click on the element in quickpick did not happen within 3 s: something drawn on top of it took the click; open on top: a quickpick | 18:35:44Z ui.sh: FAILED pick Venv --in quickpick: ... (same) | 18:35:53Z key -s=pos2: press ArrowDown then Enter to choose Venv ...
- **Fix:** It clicks a part of the row nothing covers, moving the pointer there first so no other row's tooltip opens.
- **Checked:** failed 3 of 3 tries before the fix; check.ts and all of smoke pass with it.

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

**Reason:** Helper bug in the shared lib.clickRow (scripts/page-lib.ts, old line 279: return all.nth(at).click({ timeout: 3000 })). It always clicked the row's middle. palette-run.sh leaves the pointer on the quick pick's first row; when the next picker (Python: Create Environment) draws under that resting pointer, the quick input list shows the first row's tooltip after the hover delay (upstream VS Code: quickInputList.ts _registerHoverListeners, file-origin upstream, no Positron block there), placed over the middle of the row below (on the instance: hover 538-905 x 124-149, Venv row 507-1095 x 127-149; elementFromPoint at Venv's centre was inside .workbench-hover). Playwright's hit-target check fails before it moves the mouse, so the pointer never leaves the uv row and the tooltip never goes: 'intercepts pointer events' for 3 s. Fix: clickRow finds a point on the row's middle line that elementFromPoint says belongs to the row (the centre when free, else scanning outward), moves the pointer there with page.mouse.move (so no other row's tooltip can open), checks the point again, and clicks at that position; when no point of the row is on screen (clipped or off the viewport) it clicks as before and Playwright scrolls. Valid input is unchanged: a free centre gives the same click at the centre. Helpers reached through clickRow: ui.sh pick (the finding), palette-run.sh, open-file.sh, start-session.sh, terminal-run.sh and nb.sh; I ran only ui.sh pick and palette-run.sh, which still behaves th...

**Tries:**
- finder, fail: same error; workbench-hover over the Venv row's centre
- finder, fail: same error; workbench-hover over the Venv row's centre
- fixer, fail: On my instance: palette-run 'Python: Create Environment...', then ui.sh pick Venv --in quickpick exited 1 with 'the click on the element in quickpick did not happen within 3 s: something drawn on top of it took the click; open on top: a quickpick'. The screenshot shows the uv row's tooltip over the ...

**To reproduce:**

```sh
palette-run.sh --session heal-find 'Python: Create Environment...'
ui.sh --session heal-find read quickpick
ui.sh --session heal-find pick Venv --in quickpick
shot.sh --session heal-find f8.png
```

**Commit:** 50ded66f5ceef88aed64ad56dd838bef286cf1e0

</details>

#### finder-start-session-unsupported-row: fix rejected

- **What broke:** `start-session.sh` refused to start an older Python that Positron marks "Unsupported:", saying the row was not a Python interpreter.
- **Why:** It took only rows whose name begins with "Python" as Python, and Positron puts "Unsupported:" in front of older versions.
- **In a real run:** the agent did it by hand: 18:31:27Z start-session.sh: FAILED --language python --name 'Unsupported 3.9.25 ws39' --new --timeout 60: the matching row is not a Python interpreter: Unsupported: Python 3.9.25 (uv: w... | 18:31:48Z panel.sh: delete session Unsupported: Python 3.9.25 (uv: ws39) -> deleted | 18:31:54Z palette-run.s...
- **Fix:** It treats a row named "Unsupported: Python ..." as Python, so it starts that row and lists it when --name is ambiguous.
- **Checked:** failed 3 of 3 tries; the fix was rejected: turned red: start-session --name no row matches lists the language rows (not only Python rows: ["Python 3.14.7 (uv: ws)","Python 3.14.7 (uv: root)","Python 3.13.16 (Conda: base)","Python 3.12.10 (Conda)","Python 3.13.0 (Pyenv)","Pyth); start-session several interpreters match names --name and lists ....

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

**Reason:** dp-console.ts choose() decided whether a picker row belongs to the language with label.startsWith('Python ') in three places (refusal before clicking, the 'shown' candidate list, and the 'listed' discovery test). positron-python's runtime.ts names an unsupported version's runtime `Unsupported: Python ...`, and Positron starts it, so the helper refused a valid row ('the matching row is not a Python interpreter'); with --name '3.9.25' it also filtered both 3.9 rows out of 'shown', set listed=false, retried discovery for 30 s and wrongly said no Python interpreter was listed. One local ofLanguage() test strips a leading 'Unsupported: ' and is used at all three places; only start-session.sh reaches this code (no other helper tests a runtime label's language). The prefix stays in dp-console.ts, not selectors.ts, because selectors.ts keeps label formats beside the code that parses them. Valid input behaves as before: the 'Python ' and 'R ' rows still match. Separate, not fixed here: after the uv 3.9 row started, start-session returned ok while an 'Install pip and ipykernel?' dialog still held start-up, because the console already showed '>>>'. That readiness gap would hit any interpreter without ipykernel, not just unsupported ones.

**Tries:**
- finder, fail: the matching row is not a Python interpreter: Unsupported: Python 3.9.25 (uv: ws39)
- finder, fail: same, after deleting the 3.9 session that ui.sh pick had started
- fixer, fail: On a fixture with a uv 3.9 venv in the workspace and ~/.local/bin/python3.9, the picker listed 'Unsupported: Python 3.9.25 (uv: ws)' and 'Unsupported: Python 3.9.25 (Global)'. --name 'Unsupported 3.9.25 uv' and '3.9.25 uv' failed with 'the matching row is not a Python interpreter: Unsupported: Pytho...

**To reproduce:**

```sh
shell: uv python install 3.9 && (cd <workspace> && uv venv --python 3.9 ws39)
palette-run.sh --session heal-find 'Interpreter: Start New Console Session'; quickpick-enum.sh --session heal-find   # lists 'Unsupported: Python 3.9.25 (uv: ws39)' under uv; then close the picker
start-session.sh --session heal-find --language python --name 'Unsupported 3.9.25 ws39' --new --timeout 60
start-session.sh --session heal-find --language python --name '3.9.25 ws39' --new --timeout 60
```

**Commit:** 0558a76c7c5f562e17e54a42ed5f0c6146be14cc
